## Summary

A zero-value artefact is tracked in the repository: a file literally named `=` at the repo root, whose content is a JSON dump of work item `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` (2394 bytes). It was committed by a bulk "pending working-tree changes" commit (`187cc857`) and is present in `dev`, `main`, `origin/dev` and `origin/main`. Remove it, and add a cheap regression guard so a shell-redirection typo (`cmd > =`) can never be committed again.

## Problem statement

A stray tracked file named `=` at the repo root is committed on `dev` and `main`. It is dead weight in every clone and every worktree, and it is a symptom of redirect-typo artefacts reaching the shared branches unreviewed — the same class of leak as the previously removed `node_modules` symlink and `.implement_state.json`.

## Users

- **Repository maintainers / release operators** — need a clean tracked-file surface so `git status`, audits, and release diffs stay meaningful.
- **AI agents working in worktrees** — a tracked junk file risks being "restored to HEAD" or re-committed by `git add -A` during implement runs.

Example user stories:

- As a release operator, I want `git ls-files` at the repo root to list only intentional files, so that audits and diffs are not polluted by agent-tooling debris.
- As a maintainer, I want a failing test (not tribal knowledge) to catch a future redirect-typo file, so that recurrence is caught before it reaches `dev`.

## Existing state

- `git ls-files --error-unmatch '='` succeeds; `git ls-tree` shows the file on `dev`, `main`, `origin/dev`, `origin/main`.
- Content is a JSON dump of work item `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` — evidence of a `wl show … > =` style redirect typo (the intended target was likely `>` or `=` was meant to be a variable name).
- Committed in `187cc857` ("chore: commit pending working-tree changes (AGENTS.md trim, stray wl export file)").
- Existing precedent for this class of fix: `LP-0MSI3XN6P005RO9U` (tracked `.implement_state.json` removal) and `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` (regression guard for tracked `node_modules` paths).
- No `.gitignore` rule covers shell-operator filenames today.

## Desired change

1. `git rm '='` on a feature branch and merge to `dev`; the file disappears from `main` automatically at the next `dev`→`main` release (ship skill), so no direct `main` commit is needed.
2. Add a narrow regression guard in the existing test suite that fails if a tracked path is a bare shell-redirection artefact (e.g. a repo-root filename composed only of `=`, `>`, `>>`, `|`, `<` characters, or other shell-operator-only names), with an explicit assertion that `=` is untracked. Model it on `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` (uses `git ls-files` against the live git state).
3. Deliberately **not** in scope: a `.gitignore` entry for `=` (would hide the artefact instead of failing loudly) and any change to `.githooks/pre-push` (adding a shell-level gate would require updating `tests/test_git_hooks.py` and duplicates what the pytest guard already achieves at the same dev-push gate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git ls-files --error-unmatch '='` fails (file no longer tracked) on `dev` after merge.
- [ ] Working tree no longer contains a repo-root file named `=` (`test ! -e =`), and `git status --porcelain` shows no untracked `=` residue or stray stash left behind.
- [ ] A new regression test asserts no tracked bare shell-operator filename exists at the repo root **and** that `=` specifically is untracked; the test fails if the file is re-added (`git add --intent-to-add`/re-commit simulation verified by temporarily re-adding in a scratch clone or by unit-testing the detection helper).
- [ ] The removal commit is a scoped `chore` commit — no unrelated files, no behavioural code change.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — or explicitly confirmed as N/A (no doc or comment references tracked root artefacts).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Push to `dev` only; never commit directly to `main` (the release pipeline promotes `dev`→`main`).
- Keep the change surgical: one deletion plus one small, self-contained test file; no refactoring of nearby tests.
- `git add -A` in agent flows must not resurrect the file — the removal must be committed properly, not merely deleted locally.
- Respect repository boundaries: no edits to `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Out of scope

- Broader repo-root tidy-up (e.g. the other one-off root artefacts such as `benchmark-qwen3*.json`, `eval*-report.md`) — different provenance; raise separately if wanted.
- Making the shared `implement`/worklog tooling refuse to write redirect targets — upstream framework concern, not this repo.

## Key Files

- `=` — delete; stray tracked file (JSON dump of `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR`).
- `tests/test_no_stray_root_artifacts.py` — new regression guard, modelled on `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py`.
- `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` — reference implementation / style precedent (no changes required).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the `=` file may still be reachable in `main` if the next release is delayed → mitigated by the fact that the removal rides the normal `dev`→`main` promotion; no separate `main` hotfix is warranted for a zero-impact hygiene artefact.
- **Risk:** a generic shell-operator test could false-positive on legitimate files → mitigated by restricting the guard to shell-operator-only filenames and to the repo root.
- **Risk:** scope creep into general root-file curation → explicitly out of scope (see above).
- **Assumption:** the file has no consumers (`grep` shows no references to a root file named `=`), so removal is behaviourally inert.
- **Assumption (documented, not confirmed by the producer):** a pytest regression guard is the preferred guard form over a hook or `.gitignore` rule, matching the `node_modules` precedent.

## Related work

- `LP-0MSI3XN6P005RO9U` — Remove stale tracked `.implement_state.json` from repo root (completed) — direct precedent for this class of fix.
- `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` — the work item whose JSON export leaked into the stray file (source of the artefact, not itself defective).
- `LP-0MVK0969J004MTG3` — discoverer item (`discovered-from`).
- `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` — precedent regression guard for tracked-path hygiene.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No operator interview was required: the seed context (originating from the repo inspection recorded in `LP-0MVK0969J004MTG3`) already identified the exact file, its provenance (`187cc857`), its presence on all four branches, and the intended action. Repo-first research answered the remaining questions:

- Q: "Is the file referenced anywhere (tests, scripts, docs, packaging)?" — Answer (agent, repo research): No — `git ls-files` root listing plus `grep` show no consumer; it is an orphaned redirect artefact. Source: `git show --stat 187cc857`, repo-wide `grep`.
- Q: "Does a precedent exist for removing tracked junk and guarding against recurrence?" — Answer (agent, repo research): Yes — `LP-0MSI3XN6P005RO9U` (`.implement_state.json`, `git rm` + verify) and `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` (`git ls-files` guard). Source: worklog search, file inspection.
- Q: "Is the file also on `main`, requiring a hotfix?" — Answer (agent, repo research): Yes on `main`, but the `dev`→`main` release promotion carries the removal, so no direct `main` commit is required. Source: `git ls-tree dev|main|origin/dev|origin/main -- '='`.
- Q: "Which guard form: pytest test, pre-push hook, or `.gitignore` rule?" — Answer (agent, documented assumption): pytest regression test at repo root scope; `.gitignore` would silently hide the artefact and a hook change would duplicate the dev-push gate while requiring `tests/test_git_hooks.py` updates. Flagged for producer confirmation.

# Intake brief — slot_benchmark: record finish_reason per request

**Headline:** Record each benchmark request's `finish_reason` in `slot_<N>.json`, aggregate it into `summary.finish_reason_counts` (with an explicit missing-reason count) and surface the `length` count in the human-readable summary plus the per-slot console summary, so the N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep can report the required `finish_reason=length` metric instead of "not recorded".

## Problem statement

The slot-count sweep's acceptance criteria require a `finish_reason=length` count (a smaller per-slot context at N=3/N=4 is expected to truncate more responses), but `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` records no completion reason per request — a `slot_<N>.json` request row carries only `request_index/status/total_duration_seconds/time_to_first_token_seconds/prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/tokens_per_second/resolved_model/error`. The value cannot be recovered post hoc either, because `restart_services()` truncates `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` during the restore restart, so the 2026-10-23 sweep had to record the metric as **not recorded**.

## Users

- **Producer / capacity owner** deciding `session_slot_pool_size` (keep N=2 vs move to N=3/N=4): needs the truncation count next to TTFT/decode/queue metrics to judge the per-slot-context trade-off.
  - *As a capacity owner, I want the number of truncated (`finish_reason=length`) responses per slot count so I can weigh added decode concurrency against smaller per-slot context.*
- **Benchmark operator** re-running the sweep: wants the metric in the artefacts already produced by the run, with no extra log-parsing step and no dependence on proxy logs surviving the run.
  - *As the operator, I want `summary.finish_reason_counts` in `slot_<N>.json` so the sweep evidence table can be filled in from committed artefacts alone.*

## Existing state

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py:1045` `send_request()` posts a **non-streaming** chat completion (`"stream": False`, line ~1071) and builds `RequestResult` from `usage` + `X-Resolved-Model`; the response body's `choices[0].finish_reason` is read nowhere.
- `RequestResult` (line ~541) and `SlotRunResult.summary()` (line ~603) are the two places that shape `slot_<N>.json` request rows and the per-run summary.
- `generate_report()` (line ~1414) writes `slot_benchmark_report.json` + `slot_benchmark_summary.txt`; `main()` (line ~1964) prints a per-slot inline summary.
- An in-repo precedent for the exact key name and rendering exists: `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` builds `finish_reason_counts: dict[str, int]` from `Stream finished: … reason=<x>` log lines and renders "Stream finish reasons: …".
- The gap is already documented and linked: `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` lines 232, 289–290, 365 record `finish_reason=length` as "not recorded (harness gap, LP-0MVLHNJ3W007T319)".
- Tests live in `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` (report/aggregation/CLI only; no test covers `send_request`).

## Desired change

1. Capture the reason per request in `send_request()` from the non-streaming body (`data["choices"][0].get("finish_reason")`), store it on `RequestResult` as `finish_reason: str | None` (**appended last**, so existing positional constructions stay valid), and emit it in `to_dict()`.
2. Aggregate in `SlotRunResult.summary()`: `finish_reason_counts: dict[str, int]` over completed requests, plus an explicit count of completed requests that reported no reason (absent/nullable reason reported rather than silently omitted, matching the `contention.unavailable` convention already used in this module).
3. Render it: a dedicated finish-reason block in `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` (per slot count: each reason's count, the `length` count, and the missing count) and the same information in the per-slot inline console summary. The existing main table columns stay unchanged.
4. Document the new per-request key and summary field in `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` with a `python -c` inspection snippet (mirroring the existing contention-metrics section).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `slot_<N>.json` request row carries `finish_reason`, taken from the non-streaming response body's `choices[0].finish_reason`, and `null` when the request errored (non-200/exception) or the provider returned no reason — verified by unit tests that stub the HTTP response.
2. `summary.finish_reason_counts` (present in `slot_<N>.json`, in `slot_benchmark_report.json` `runs[].summary`, and in the in-memory `SlotRunResult.summary()`) maps each observed reason to its count over completed requests, so a truncation count is readable directly as `summary.finish_reason_counts["length"]`, and completed requests with no recorded reason are counted explicitly (not dropped).
3. `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` contains a finish-reason section reporting, per slot count, each reason's count including `length` and the missing-reason count (with `--`/explicit wording when no run recorded any), and the per-slot inline console summary prints the same finish-reason line — both asserted by tests reading the generated artefacts.
4. `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` documents the new per-request `finish_reason` key, the `summary.finish_reason_counts` field and the missing-reason count, including a runnable `python -c` snippet that prints the per-slot reason counts from `slot_benchmark_report.json`.
5. `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` gains tests covering: `send_request` capture of a present reason, a missing/null reason (counted as missing), an error request (`finish_reason` is `null`), mixed-reason aggregation in `summary()`, and the summary-file/console rendering — and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No streaming capture path is required.** The harness only issues non-streaming requests (`stream: False`); the streaming variant named in the seed description does not exist in this file. Adding a streaming mode is out of scope (see Assumptions).
- **Backwards compatibility of the artefacts and dataclass:** `RequestResult` is constructed positionally in existing tests and `summary` keys are consumed by `compare_results.py`-style delta comparisons — append the new field last with a default and do not rename/remove existing summary keys or main-table columns.
- **No new production instrumentation, no proxy changes** — the metric comes from the benchmark's own HTTP responses.
- **Do not backfill historical runs.** `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/` cannot be repaired (the restore restart cleared the proxy log); `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` is a historical record and stays as-is (it already links this item as the gap).
- Marker for "no reason recorded" must be distinguishable from reason `"stop"`/`"length"` — do not conflate absent with a fabricated default.
- Restyling/renumbering the existing human-readable report sections is out of scope (only additive changes plus the one console line).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — non-streaming only:** `send_request()` fixes `stream: False`; the non-streaming `choices[0].finish_reason` is the correct capture point. If a streaming harness is added later, a follow-up item must extend the capture to the last streamed chunk.
- **Assumption — key naming:** `finish_reason_counts` is reused verbatim from `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` so slot evidence tables and extract reports read consistently.
- **Assumption — absence is reported, not guessed:** completed requests with no `finish_reason` are counted separately; the sweep reading rule (only meaningful for locally served requests) is documented rather than enforced.
- **Risk — misleading `length` counts under remote fallback:** a remote provider may report `stop` for a response the local slot would have truncated, so `finish_reason_counts` must be read together with the existing `contention.local_stream_share` (and per-request `resolved_model`). *Mitigation:* AC4 documentation states this reading rule; no per-provider cross-tab is added (scope control).
- **Risk — artefact consumers:** a renamed/removed summary key or a widened main table could break delta comparisons in existing result notes. *Mitigation:* additive-only change (new field appended, new section, existing columns untouched).
- **Risk — scope creep:** per-provider `length` cross-tabs, streaming capture, historical backfill and a proxy-side `finish_reason` metric are all plausible follow-ons. *Mitigation:* they are explicitly out of scope here and should be recorded as linked items if wanted, not folded in.
- **Risk — the metric alone does not unblock the sweep:** the 2026-10-23 runs were also INVALID on local concurrency (`LP-0MVLHNEDO008FTBH`), so this item removes one blocker but does not by itself make the sweep decision-ready.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — Needs `RequestResult.finish_reason` (+`to_dict`), capture in `send_request()`, `finish_reason_counts` + missing count in `SlotRunResult.summary()`, a finish-reason section in `generate_report()`, and one extra line in the per-slot inline summary in `main()`.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` — Needs new tests for capture (stubbed `httpx` response), absence/error handling, aggregation and rendering.
- `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` — Needs documentation of the new per-request key, summary field, reading rule (pair with `local_stream_share`) and an inspection snippet.
- `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` — No change expected; reference implementation for the `finish_reason_counts` naming/rendering convention.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVK09622002CRMR` — Record slot-count verdict and reconcile with projection (discovered-from; its AC1 evidence table requires the `finish_reason=length` count).
- `LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD` — Run controlled N=3/N=4 slot-count sweep in a quiet window (parent epic of the predecessor).
- `LP-0MVK096GF0038FTH` — Execute N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep in a quiet window (the run that recorded the metric as "not recorded").
- `LP-0MVLHNEDO008FTBH` — Slot-sweep harness cannot exercise local concurrency: add a warm-start / staggered-arrival mode (parallel harness gap; listed as a precondition alongside this item).
- `LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8` — Re-evaluate `session_slot_pool_size` against measured GPU busy-time and contention history (defines the metric set; its doc records this gap).
- `LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC` — prefill-aware busy metrics (sibling metric gap for the same sweep).
- `LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD` — Slot-count benchmark: find optimal `session_slot_pool_size` for Qwen3 (original harness item).
- `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` + `tests/test_slot_history_extract.py` — existing `finish_reason_counts` implementation to mirror.
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` — records this harness gap and its effect on the 2026-10-23 verdict (`finish_reason=length` → not testable).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were required for this intake — the seed description (a `discovered-from` follow-up) fully specifies the desired capture, aggregation keys and rendering, and the residual decisions were resolvable by repo inspection. Decisions taken (recorded as assumptions above), with evidence:

- **Q (self-answered): Is a streaming capture path needed?** — Answer (agent, repo evidence): No. `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py:1071` sets `"stream": False` and builds the result from `resp.json()`; there is no streaming code path in this harness. Capture point is `choices[0].finish_reason`. Source: file inspection.
- **Q (self-answered): Which summary key name?** — Answer (agent, repo evidence): `finish_reason_counts`, matching `scripts/slot_history_extract.py:386/560/768` (`finish_reason_counts` + "Stream finish reasons" rendering). Source: file inspection.
- **Q (self-answered): How is a missing reason represented?** — Answer (agent, convention): explicitly counted (absent ≠ fabricated default), matching the module's existing "absent metrics are reported explicitly" convention (`ContentionMetrics.unavailable`). Source: `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` contention-metrics section.
- **Q (self-answered): Are historical runs backfilled or the reevaluation doc updated?** — Answer (agent): No. `restart_services()` clears the proxy log, so the 2026-10-23 metric is unrecoverable; the reevaluation doc is a historical record that already links this item (`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md:232,289,365`).

# Goal

Close out the observational acceptance criteria of **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (false `saturated` capacity signal) once the new proxy code is running on `dev`.

## Background

The gate-side fix (commits 56a3a28a, 2d2b6b51) makes `/llama/local/status` truthful: stale slot detail degrades `capacity_hint` to `idle` (never `saturated`) without live work; `local_active_query` is derived from active dispatch records; an unloaded model (HTTP 400/404 from llama-server's router `/slots?model=`) is treated as fresh absence (fail open on the pool); and `local_prefills_in_flight` publishes only markers backed by a live record.

What cannot be verified inside the implementation session is the overnight behaviour.

## Problem statement

The capacity-signal fix is merged, but its real-world effect on the overnight herdr downtime dispatcher and on `/llama/local/status` staleness is unmeasured. Without a post-fix measurement over a comparable night window we cannot confirm the false-`saturated` starvation is resolved.

## Users

- **Operator/maintainer of the local LLM proxy** — needs confidence that overnight idle GPU capacity is actually used by the herdr downtime dispatcher.
  - As the operator, I want the post-fix `slots_stale` poll rate to be well under the pre-fix 79.5% so I know status is truthful.
  - As the operator, I want herdr downtime dispatches on an idle night to return to the Oct 20/21 baseline (>=10/night) so idle GPU time is not wasted.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Over a night window comparable to 2026-10-22 (20:00-07:00 local), `slots_stale` is <5% of status polls (was 79.5%), and `capacity_hint=saturated` is only observed while the proxy has live local work.
- AC2: herdr downtime dispatches on a genuinely idle GPU night reach the Oct 20/21 baseline (>=10 dispatches/night) with the same work-item queue (was 1 in ~9 h).
- AC3: Any residual stale polls are attributable (documented cause, e.g. transient /slots 500 vs idle-model unload) in the nightly usage report.
- AC4: Report the measured numbers on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM and close this item.
- AC5: The measurement is reproducible/validated — the derivation of each reported figure (poll counts, `slots_stale` rate, `capacity_hint` distribution, dispatch count) is documented with the exact log files and commands/logic used, so a reviewer can re-derive the numbers.
- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the nightly usage report and `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` reflect the post-fix findings.
- AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement work: do not change proxy behaviour or dispatch logic in this item.
- Window is fixed: 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 IST (Europe/Dublin); the fix was live from ~10:35 IST on 2026-10-24.
- Evidence lives in `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.*` and `~/proxy-usage-reports/`; use the nightly usage report where available rather than ad-hoc parsing where the report already covers it.
- Never kill the proxy to collect evidence; use logs only.

## Existing state

Pre-fix evidence (2026-10-22 night): `slots_stale=true` on 7,543 of 9,484 polls (79.5%); `capacity_hint=saturated` on 7,807 of 9,484 polls (82.3%); 100% of 02:00/03:00 polls saturated while zero local streams ran; herdr dispatched 1 work item in ~9 h vs 14–15/night on Oct 20/21.

## Desired change

Post-fix measurement over the fixed window, recorded as a report: `slots_stale` poll rate (<5% target), `capacity_hint` distribution while idle (saturated only with live work), herdr downtime dispatch count (>=10 target), and attribution of any residual stale polls. Findings reported on the parent item LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.*` — primary evidence: status polls, `slots_stale`, `capacity_hint`, dispatch records for the window.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` — nightly usage report output (per-day directories) used as the canonical report surface.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — deterministic analyzer for proxy usage/error taxonomy.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` — status contract to reconcile observed `capacity_hint`/`slots_stale` semantics.
- Parent item `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — destination for the reported numbers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** proxy logs for the full window are retained (confirmed present: `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22`, `proxy.log-2026-10-25_00`, `proxy.log`).
- **Assumption:** herdr downtime dispatch counts are reconstructable from proxy logs/or herdr decision logs.
- **Risk:** residual stale polls may be un-attributable if log detail is insufficient — AC3 requires documenting cause, or explicitly stating the cause could not be determined.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any new defect found during measurement (e.g. a distinct status bug) should be filed as a linked work item, not fixed here.

## Related work

- Parent fix: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (discovered-from)
- Evidence window: `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` (2026-10-23 05:00 run), `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.*`
- Status contract: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** – Bug: Stale Local Dispatch Lease Blocks Subsequent Local Requests (completed)
- **LP-0MTYL5K1S002M5QL** – Reclaim stale generating counters in cleanup loop (completed)
- **LP-0MRNV040H0055N2Q** – [test-failure] test_stub_router_integration — flaky test-ordering-dependent assert ok Failure (completed)

## Plan

Decomposed into three dependency-ordered children (test-first: verification tooling before measurement, documentation/close-out last). Effort/risk on this item: **Small / Medium** (approval gate not triggered). All seven acceptance criteria are mapped to a child AC.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Covers parent ACs |
|---|-------|------|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | `LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK` — Capacity-signal verification tool: reproducible window metrics | task (verification, test-first) | — | AC5 (+AC7 test part) |
| 2 | `LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV` — Measure post-fix night window: stale rate, capacity_hint, dispatch count | task | 1 | AC1, AC2, AC3 |

### Reuse (no new wheel)

- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — rotation/gzip-aware log discovery (dot + dash names, `.gz`), per-line window filtering, and a coverage verdict that fails on gaps.

### Evidence coverage (verified during planning)

The fixed window 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 IST is fully covered by rotated logs: `proxy.log.2026-10-24_17.gz` (20:00→23:37), `proxy.log-2026-10-25_00` (23:37→23:59), `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22` (00:00→04:37), `proxy.log.2026-10-25_04` (04:37→07:00). `slots_stale` lines are present in the window files (e.g. 5,325 matches in `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22`).

### Phasing

Each child is a vertical slice: the tool child delivers script + unit tests + docstring derivation; the measurement child delivers numbers + artifacts; the close-out child delivers report + docs + suite gate. The plan needs no further phasing.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 (plan skill, Map): created children LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK, LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV, LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23; wired deps 2→1 and 3→2; restated parent ACs literally in child ACs to satisfy the AC-coverage review (Jaccard ≥ 0.4, coverage 100%); verified log coverage for the fixed window; stage → `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Was the item sufficiently defined to skip the intake interview?" — Answer (Map, agent): "Yes — the item already had a clear goal, background, four measurable ACs and references, and is a small `task`. Per intake Step 1 heuristics it qualified for auto-complete; no interview questions were required." Source: `wl show LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 --json` inspection at intake.

- Q: "Is the exact log source / file-to-window mapping for `slots_stale` and `capacity_hint` known?" — Answer (Map, agent, resolved from evidence rather than by asking): "Yes. Rotated files map to the window as recorded in the Plan section; `slots_stale` appears in the window files. The plan therefore includes a coverage verdict in the tool so a gap can never read as a partial success." Evidence: `zcat -f /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.* | grep -c slots_stale` over the 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-24/25 files; first/last timestamps of each file.
- Q: "Should the derivation be a new tool or ad-hoc parsing?" — Answer (Map, agent): "New reproducible tool at `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`, because parent AC5 requires re-derivable figures; reuse `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (discovery/coverage) and follow `scripts/dispatch_latency_verification.py`. The tool is validated by reproducing the pre-fix 2026-10-22 baseline (79.5% stale / 82.3% saturated) as a control."
- Q: "Where do the post-fix findings get recorded?" — Answer (Map, agent): "Numbers + attribution on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (parent AC4), plus `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` and the nightly usage report for the window (parent AC6)."

### OPEN QUESTION (directed to: operator; matters for parent AC6 scope)

The nightly usage report is produced by `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (agent infrastructure). Parent AC6 says the nightly report must "reflect the post-fix findings". If that requires adding `slots_stale` rate / `capacity_hint` distribution to the report generator itself, that is a change under `.pi/`, which the repository-boundary rule forbids without explicit instruction. Default plan: document the findings in `~/proxy-usage-reports/` content for the window and in `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`; if the generator needs changing, the close-out child records it as an Open Question and files a separate work item rather than editing `.pi/` unilaterally.

### Assumptions recorded during planning

- The pre-fix control window (2026-10-22 20:00→07:00) is deliberately re-measured by the same tool; a mismatch beyond the documented tolerance means the method is wrong, not that the fix failed.
- "Live local work" for the saturated-with-live-work check is derived from proxy dispatch records in the same logs (active dispatch windows), not from GPU metrics.
- herdr downtime dispatch count is derivable from proxy logs; if it is not, the measurement child must state the limitation explicitly (parent AC3 allows "could not be determined").

## Goal (user story)

As an operator of the LLM proxy, I want the 24-hour usage report to include a
"local-turn coverage" section so I can see which sessions actually used the
local LLM, how many turns it answered, what share of the session's turns were
local, and why each session moved to remote — so I can judge whether local is
under-utilised and why.

## Context

The delivered analysis (24h window 2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52)
showed that 26 of 175 sessions had at least one turn routed to local, and all
225 such turns were answered (100% completion: 214 tool_calls, 10 stop,
1 length). 149 sessions never used local. A proposed section renders this as
three deterministic tables:

1. **Summary table** — rows P10 / P50 / P90 (+ totals) over the sessions with
   ≥1 local turn, columns: # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns,
   context size at fallback. Sorted by # turns local ascending in the
   percentile rows, more local turns being the goal. Session ID and fallback
   reason are categorical and therefore excluded from the percentile table;
   the reason distribution is provided as its own counts-and-% table (2).
2. **Fallback-reason summary table** — one row per fallback reason with a
   count and a % of the sessions-with-local (P50 # turns local 4.5, # turns
   remote 14.5, % local turns 26.2%; reference-window reason tally below).
3. **Per-session sampling table** — every session with ≥1 local turn,
   columns: session ID, # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns, reason
   for remote fallback, context size at fallback; sorted by # turns local
   descending (more local = better, best first). 26 rows in the reference
   window. % local turns = local / (local + remote) × 100 per session.

Operational definitions:

- "Routed to local for at least 1 turn and receives a response": a local
  `Stream started` (provider=local) paired with a local `Stream finished`
  (provider=local). All 225 routed turns were answered in the reference
  window; a routed-but-errored turn (Stream finished reason=error) would be
  counted as routed but flagged as unanswered rather than dropped.
- "% local turns": per-session share of turns answered by local
  (local / (local + remote), null when a session has no remote turns →
  100%). Percentiles of this column use linear interpolation like the others.
- "Context size at fallback": `estimated_tokens` from the session's
  `routing_skip_local` line at/near its recorded fallback (remote_move_time),
  falling back to the first remote stream's prompt tokens, and finally to
  start_context_size/max_context_size from the session CSV. Sessions whose
  log lines carry no `tokens=` value render an explicit n/a (3 of 26 in the
  reference window: empty_response / fallback_after_queue sessions) — never a
  fabricated estimate.
- Fallback reason: the session's existing attributed fallback_reason,
  sourced from the session's OWN evidence only (current report contract,
  LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES): own routing_skip_local first, else own
  routing_skip_provider_context, else own Fallback triggered, else — only
  for rotated logs predating the session stamp — the nearest session-less
  fallback line within 60s. Explicit states: `no_remote_fallback`,
  `lease_denied` (local_lease_active refusal), `unattributed` (no own
  evidence). A session's reason is never inherited from an unrelated
  neighbour's global fallback line.

Reference-window fallback-reason tally (26 sessions): rate_limited 11
(42.3%), no remote fallback 4 (15.4%), empty_response 3 (11.5%),
provider_context_exceeded 2 (7.7%), local_concurrency_limit 2 (7.7%), and one
each (3.8%) of HTTP 503, fallback_after_queue, large_context_bypass,
context_too_large.

Notable findings the section should surface as interpretation notes:

- Context-size fallbacks never occur on a session's first message (median
  first-message prompt ~29.6K tokens vs cold_threshold 38000 / warm_threshold
  120000); they fire only after context grows past the thresholds. Reference
  window: 0 of 5268 local-to-remote fallbacks were first-message.
- 96.6% of local-to-remote fallbacks happen before the session has produced
  any local work (routing is decision-first, so local is declined
  pre-emptively, not after a failed attempt).
- rate_limited is the proxy's own per-provider RPM budget pacing
  (provider_budget.py BudgetDecision reason=rate_limited: the configured
  rate_limit_rpm window for that provider entry is exhausted and the request
  is passed through to the next provider immediately), NOT an upstream HTTP
  429 — those surface as upstream_http_error status=429 events instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: report.md contains a deterministic "Local model usage by session"
  section with the summary percentile table (P10/P50/P90 + total row over
  sessions with ≥1 local turn in the window) using the column set: # turns
  local, # turns remote, % local turns, context size at fallback.
- AC2: The section contains the fallback-reason counts-and-% summary table
  (reason, count, % of sessions-with-local).
- AC3: The section contains a per-session table listing each session with ≥1
  local turn: session ID, # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns,
  reason for remote fallback, context size at fallback; sorted by # turns
  local descending.
- AC4: Context size at fallback derives from routing_skip_local
  estimated_tokens at/near the session's fallback (falling back to the first
  remote stream's prompt tokens, then session CSV context columns); sessions
  without any token data render "n/a" with a limitation note, never a
  fabricated estimate.
- AC5: The section renders from the existing log/config inputs only (no new
  data sources); the per-session data is present in the session CSVs or an
  explicitly documented new artifact.
- AC6: Rule-based tests cover: session selection (≥1 local turn answered),
  percentile computation (P10/P50/P90, linear interpolation), % local turns
  derivation, fallback attribution (reason + context at fallback), the
  fallback-reason counts-and-% table, sort order, and the no-tokens n/a
  limitation path.
- AC7: The full suite passes via the test skill; the daily 05:00 cron run
  includes the new section with no agent in the loop.

## References

- Reference numbers (window 2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52): 26/175
  sessions with ≥1 local turn; 225 local turns, 225 answered; P50 local
  turns 4.5, P50 remote turns 14.5, P50 % local turns 26.2%, P50 context at
  fallback ~11K tokens; totals 225 local / 663 remote turns (25.3% local
  overall).
- Skill: .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis (SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md, scripts/).


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25T03:2xZ (plan skill; session herdr-1792897925-2552737-30168):
  pre-check returned `skip` (effort Extra Small, risk Low) — auto-plan path:
  six-stage review only; no child items created.
- Corrected the fallback-reason operational definition to the implemented
  attribution contract (LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES, completed): the prior wording
  ("own routing_skip_first, else nearest Fallback triggered within 60s")
  described the pre-fix attribution that inherited an unrelated neighbour's
  line (11/26 local-using sessions mislabelled as rate_limited in the
  reference window) and contradicted the analysis comment on this item.
- OPEN QUESTION (for implementer / producer): the description's
  reference-window numbers — 26/175 sessions, the fallback-reason tally
  (rate_limited 11, 42.3%; no remote fallback 4, 15.4%; etc.) and the P50
  context-at-fallback figure (~11K tokens) — were computed under the
  pre-fix nearest-line attribution. Recompute the reference numbers from
  real logs under the current attribution contract before finalising the
  section; treat the description's tally as indicative, not authoritative,
  when validating the new section's output.
data.title: Add local-turn coverage report to proxy usage analysis skill

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy maintainer, I want the unused `github` model chain (and its
`github-primary` provider entry) removed from `proxy/config.yaml`, so the
configuration reflects reality and carries no dead routing surface that could
silently attract traffic or confuse future readers.

## Evidence that it is unused

- `proxy/config.yaml` lines ~346-352 declare a `models.github` chain with a
  single remote provider `github-primary` (endpoint
  `https://models.inference.ai.azure.com`, aliases `github-*`).
- Zero traffic in every available proxy log (2026-10-17 14:46 → 2026-10-24
  10:35): no `provider=GitHub`, no `entry=github`, no `github-primary`, no
  `models.inference.ai` occurrences.
- In the 24h usage window (2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52) only three
  initial providers appear across 175 sessions: OpenCode, MunitoAI, and
  local/Qwen3.
- No test in tests/ or proxy/tests/ references the github chain.
- The only other reference is documentation: docs/routing.md:297 notes
  `github-primary` is deliberately ungated (no `model` declared). That note
  must be removed/updated with the chain.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `github` chain (provider entry `github-primary` and its
  `github-*` aliases) is removed from proxy/config.yaml; no other chain
  references it.
- AC2: The resulting config loads cleanly — proxy startup/config-load tests
  pass, and a config validation/merge test confirms no dangling alias or
  provider reference remains.
- AC3: Documentation is consistent: docs/routing.md no longer describes
  `github-primary` as an ungated provider (remove the paragraph or restate it
  for a surviving ungated entry), and any config header comment naming it is
  updated.
- AC4: A regression test asserts the `github` chain is absent (config-load
  test), so the dead entry cannot be reintroduced unnoticed.
- AC5: If any client is found to request a `github-*` model alias (grep of
  shipped client configs), that must be reported and resolved before removal
  — otherwise AC1/AC4 stand.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill before the change is closed.

## Notes

- The upstream model is unreachable anyway: `github-primary` declares no
  `model`, so the client chooses it; nothing in this deployment exercises
  that path. Removal also drops the "deliberately NOT gated" special case in
  the max_context_tokens documentation block (config.yaml ~line 324).
- Related: model chains shipped after removal are `embed`, `private`, `plan`,
  `author`, `code`, `compact`.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and analyst, I want a single per-turn correlation identifier
carried on every structured log line, so a request's full lifecycle — local
routing decision, fallbacks, stream start, stream finish, tokens — can be
reconstructed exactly instead of by FIFO pairing and nearest-line heuristics.

## Why

Today a turn leaves a trail of lines tied together only by session UUID and
timestamp ordering: `routing_skip_local` -> `Fallback triggered` xN ->
`Stream started` -> `Stream finished`. The analysis skill compensates with
heuristics (FIFO stream pairing, 60s fallback windows, nearest-attribution)
that mis-assign reasons (see the rate_limited misattribution in the
2026-10-23/24 window, where a session's own lease denials were overwritten by
an unrelated session's fallback line). A per-request id would remove every
one of these heuristics.

## Design note (plan in implementation)

Emitting an id at the earliest point a request is known (accept/entry) and
carrying it on: `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`,
`Fallback triggered`, `routing_hop`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `[local]/[remote]
POST`, `Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `dispatch_first_byte_ms=`,
`ttft_seconds=`, and the error lines. Short (e.g. 8-hex) to keep lines
readable; both local and remote paths are in different modules
(`proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy_remote.py`), so this is
a cross-cutting change with a shared helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A shared helper (e.g. in `proxy/utils.py` or a new module) generates
  and stamps a per-turn id, and the id is carried on all structured line
  kinds listed above (verify each emit site; no line kind may be left with
  the id unconditionally absent).
- AC2: The id is stable across the full lifecycle of one client request —
  including across fallback hops and chain-hold re-emissions — and unique per
  turn of a session (at minimum within the session).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill consumes the id:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  relevant events; `aggregation.py` pairs streams, fallbacks, skips and TTFT
  events by id (falling back to today's heuristics only when the id is
  absent in older logs); `reporting.py` documents that per-turn attribution is
  exact where ids exist.
- AC4: Skill tests: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` lines with ids; new tests prove
  exact pairing by id (fallback -> stream, skip -> stream, TTFT -> stream)
  and that legacy lines without ids still parse via the existing fallback
  paths.
- AC5: Proxy tests asserting log text are updated where they instantiate or
  assert these lines: `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`.
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`; the pass-through log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` is verified unaffected.
- AC7: Documentation: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` documents the id field and the
  exact-attribution semantics; SKILL.md notes no behavioural change.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill; no regression in the deterministic
  daily report path.

## Notes

- This supersedes most of the pairing heuristics in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`; the change is cross-cutting, so split
  into sub-tasks during planning (shared helper + emit sites; parsers; skill
  consumption; tests) if useful.
- Backwards compatibility mandatory: old logs without ids must keep parsing.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25: Pre-check returned `skip` (Extra Small, Low risk). Ran six automated review stages. Corrected AC4 `tests/fixtures.py` → `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, AC7 `REFERENCE.md` → `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`. Plan complete — item ready for implementation.
data.title: Add per-turn correlation id to all structured log lines

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy-usage analyst, I want `Stream finished` lines to say explicitly
when an upstream reported no token usage, so "no data" is distinguishable from
"zero tokens" and sessions with unknown context are countable rather than
invisible.

## Why

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` only appends `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
when the upstream response carries a `usage` object:

```
if isinstance(usage, dict): ... parts.append(f"tokens=...")
```

When a provider (or an aborted/errored stream) omits usage, the line silently
has no `tokens=` field. In the 2026-10-23/24 window this left 3 of the 26
local-using sessions with no context size at all (their `Stream finished`
lines carry no tokens), so any analysis of "context at fallback" for them
degrades to n/a with no way to tell why at the log level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a terminal stream has no reportable usage, the `Stream finished`
  line carries an explicit marker (e.g. `tokens=missing` or `usage=none`),
  emitted from the same code path in `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`.
- AC2: The marker never overrides real usage — a present `usage` object still
  logs `tokens=p/c/t` exactly as today (no format change for the populated
  case).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill counts the new marker:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  stream-finished event, and `aggregation.py`/`reporting.py` report a
  "streams without usage" count (window-level, and per-session where the
  context-at-fallback table is rendered) instead of silently emitting n/a.
- AC4: `reporting.py` limitation text in the affected sections names the
  marker as the cause of missing context figures.
- AC5: Tests: a fixture line with `tokens=missing` in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, plus tests in
  `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` proving (a) missing-usage streams are counted
  and excluded from token totals, and (b) populated lines are unchanged.
  Proxy-side test for the emit path in `proxy/tests/` (whichever suite covers
  `router_helpers` stream-finish logging).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (any code doing
  `tokens=` regex matches must not treat `missing` as a number).
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the marker and its meaning.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — emit path for the `tokens=missing` marker (AC1, AC2, AC5).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — parses the marker onto the stream-finished event (AC3).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — "streams without usage" count (AC3).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — count in report + limitation text (AC3, AC4).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixture line with `tokens=missing` (AC5).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — analyser tests for the marker (AC5).
- `proxy/tests/test_stream_entry_name_logging.py` — proxy-side tests for the emit path (AC5).
- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` — consumer audit: `tokens=` regex must not treat `missing` as a number (AC6).
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` — documents the marker and its meaning (AC7).

## Notes

- Small, contained change; the risk is consumers that regex
  `tokens=(\d+)/(\d+)/(\d+)` — those simply won't match the marker, which is
  the desired behaviour, but each should be verified rather than assumed.
data.title: Emit explicit tokens=missing marker when upstream reports no usage

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the proxy's own request-budget skip to use a name that
cannot be confused with an upstream rate-limit rejection, so operators and
analysis tooling stop misreading `rate_limited` as "the local model was rate
limited".

## Why

`rate_limited` is emitted by `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` when a provider
entry's configured `rate_limit_rpm` window is exhausted
(`BudgetDecision(reason="rate_limited")`). It is a **proxy-side, pre-flight
budget skip**, not an HTTP 429 from the provider — upstream 429s are logged
separately as `[remote] upstream error status=429` /
`upstream_http_error`.

The name caused a concrete misreading: `rate_limited` is 61.6% of the
fallback-reason table (6,042 events, all `from=munitoai-free`), yet it was
reported as the per-session "reason for remote fallback" for 11 of 26
sessions that had actually been diverted from local by lease contention. The
local provider has no `rate_limit_rpm` and can never emit this reason (0 of
9,683 archive occurrences are `from=local`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The budget-skip vocabulary is renamed to
  `provider_budget_exhausted`, everywhere it is emitted: the
  `BudgetDecision.reason` values in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
  (retaining the `_after_wait` / `_waiters` / `_disconnect` variants, e.g.
  `provider_budget_exhausted_after_wait`), the `reason=` text in the
  `Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=...` log lines, the
  `fallback_reason = ...` assignments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  (~9028, ~10515), **and the diagnostics attempt `status` values**
  `status="rate_limited"` / `status="rate_limited_waited"` (~9018, ~9038,
  ~10505, ~10525) -> `status="provider_budget_exhausted"` /
  `status="provider_budget_exhausted_waited"`. Producer decision
  (2026-10-25): *full rename everywhere* — no `rate_limited*` literal may
  remain in **newly emitted** code paths, tests, or current documentation.
  The analysis-skill legacy mapping (AC3) and `REFERENCE.md` deliberately
  retain the old spelling as a *historical* name (exactly as
  `warm_cache_bypass` is retained next to `context_too_large`).
- AC2: Internal decisions/behaviour are unchanged: the affinity/reserve/wait
  logic and any cooldown behaviour keep working (the rename must not alter
  decisions — it is a string rename only). `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` is updated
  to key on the new status (`frozenset({"provider_budget_exhausted"})`,
  provider.py ~4181); `status_code=429` in the diagnostic attempt entries
  stays as-is (a numeric HTTP code, not the reason vocabulary); the
  reason-keyed budget-evidence gate `(reason or "").startswith("rate_limited")`
  (~669) switches to the new prefix.
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill normalises legacy logs: `log_parser.py` maps
  `rate_limited*` -> `provider_budget_exhausted*` so historical windows and
  new windows report under one label, with the mapping documented in
  `REFERENCE.md` (add to the existing legacy reason mapping next to
  `warm_cache_bypass` -> `context_too_large`).
- AC4: `reporting.py` renders the new label and keeps the reason table stable
  (no duplicate rows for old/new names in one window);
  `recommendations.py` text that references rate limiting is updated to
  distinguish proxy budget pacing from upstream 429s. Paths verified at plan
  time: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` (legend at
  ~line 545) and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
  (~lines 478, 544, 731).
- AC5: Tests: parser normalisation tests (old and new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; every test that asserts the old
  reason string is updated. Audited set (verified at plan time by literal
  scan): `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (20 occurrences — the primary
  decision-reason tests), `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_budget_eval_parse.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py`, `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`,
  `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`.
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py` were named in the original
  draft but contain **no** `rate_limited` literal — confirmed listed in error
  (producer decision 2026-10-25), nothing to change there.
  With the full rename the attempt-`status` assertions also move:
  `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (~1187), `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`
  (~75, ~169, ~397), `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py` (~357),
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` (~360). Test-function names describing the
  old vocabulary are renamed in the same change (see implementation notes).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want local prompt-eval (prefill) throughput increased so that
large cold prompts become cheap enough to serve locally, unlocking real local
utilisation instead of diverting work to paid remote providers.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This item must only be executed once we have had a successful night of local
LLM consumption, meaning >60% GPU utilisation across a full night.** Until
local actually carries sustained work (>60% local busy), tuning prefill
throughput is premature: there is no sustained workload to measure against and
no evidence that prefill latency — rather than routing policy — is the binding
constraint. Verify the gate with the `proxy-usage-analysis` report's
`## Local model utilization` section for a night window (e.g. 22:00-07:00):
it must show busy >= 60%. Record that evidence in a comment on this item
before starting work; if the gate is not met, leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Prompt-eval speed (llama-server eval timing, Qwen3, fast bucket): median
  **90.7 tok/s**, p90 316.7, p10 24.9 (532 samples, 24h window
  2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52).
- Per-stream prefill (dispatch -> first byte): p50 4.4s, p90 35.3s, max 73.7s.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` — a slow prefill can be cancelled, and
  prior incidents show cancelled prefills re-dispatching identical prompts
  (the prefill-thrash cooldown exists because of this).
- The prefill-ETA admission guard refused **478** local admissions in the
  window on projected prefill cost, and only **34** requests were admitted by
  the idle override despite local being idle 89.8% of the time.
- Current llama-server launch flags (Qwen3 child):
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024
  --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
  --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation
  for a full night, taken from the usage-analysis report, before any change is
  made. Work does not start without it.
- AC1: A measured baseline is captured first: prompt-eval tok/s distribution
  (p10/p50/p90), prefill phase duration, prefill-ETA admission refusals, and
  prefill-thrash events over a fixed window, all from the
  `proxy-usage-analysis` artifacts.
- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch
  configuration (candidates: `--ubatch-size` 1024 -> 2048/4096, `--batch-size`,
  `--mlock`, thread count, SWA/checkpoint settings) and/or the prefill-related
  proxy knobs (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, the ETA guard budget). Each
  changed value is justified by measurement, not by guesswork.
- AC3: The optimisation is measured with the same method as AC1 and the
  before/after comparison is recorded on this item, including any effect on
  decode speed (no regression to decode tok/s median) and on stability
  (`slot_save failed`, prefill cancellations, HTTP 400/503 rates).
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's
  configuration and documentation are updated together, and the
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill is updated if new or changed log evidence is
  needed to measure the improvement
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{llama_log_parser.py,log_parser.py,
  reporting.py}`, `REFERENCE.md`), and any other log-consuming script that
  reads llama-server eval timings or prefill evidence is audited
  (`proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_lease_verification.py`).
- AC6: Launch-flag changes are documented in `models.ini` / start-proxy
  documentation so the settings are reproducible, and any start-proxy script
  or test asserting the flags is updated.
- AC7: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- This item is downstream of routing policy: raising local demand (thresholds,
  serve-first admission) comes first, otherwise there is nothing to optimise
  for. Keep the gate.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (evaluate increasing local ctx-size) and the
  slot-geometry experiment (1 slot vs 2) — decide ctx/slot geometry before
  micro-tuning batch sizes, since the two interact.

## Plan (2026-10-25)

Decomposed into nine children. Every change-making child is dependency-blocked
on the **gate child** (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ, *Verify sustained local utilisation gate*) and on the gated geometry experiment
(LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN), so nothing starts before AC0 is satisfied. This item
itself depends on the gate child and therefore renders as `blocked`.

| # | Child | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verify sustained local utilisation gate (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ) | AC0 | — |
| 2 | Baseline prefill measurement capture (LP-0MVNBJWRH006V9Y6) | AC1 | 1 |
| 3 | 40-80k prefill benchmark capability (LP-0MVNBJX3G008IBTB) | AC2 (measurement validity) | 1, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 4 | Measurement evidence and log-consumer audit (LP-0MVNBJXF9002DJAZ) | AC5 | 1, 2 |
| 5 | Launch-flag A/B: ubatch and batch size (LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD) | AC2 | 1, 2, 3, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 6 | Launch-flag A/B: threads and SWA checkpoints (LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51) | AC2 | 1, 5 |
| 7 | ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review (LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J) | AC2 (proxy knobs), AC4 | 1, 2, 5, 6 |
| 8 | Post-change verification: latency and stability (LP-0MVNBJYPM004UV56) | AC3, AC7 | 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 |
| 9 | Document launch flags and reproducibility (LP-0MVNBJZ100020UN0) | AC6 | 1, 5, 6 |

Sequence: gate -> baseline + harness capability (test-first) -> launch-flag
A/B -> guard review -> post-change verification + docs. Each child is a
vertical slice carrying its own tests, config/docs change and measurement
record.

Vertical-slice decision: the change is deliberately **not** phased into
separate "code" and "docs" phases; each A/B child lands flag + test + comment
together, because an undocumented or untested flag change is not deliverable.

**Effort/risk (this plan):** Medium (`recommended 51.22 h`, range 33.3-76.0 h)
/ **Medium** (score 10). Estimate source: `effort-and-risk` skill with this
plan's per-child WBS; it replaces the `0.00 h` autoplan placeholder recorded
earlier.

**Gate status at planning time:** NOT met (busy 2.2 % for the night
2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00; 10.2 % over the 24 h daily report).
Children that change configuration must not start until AC0 is satisfied.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Answered by repository / work-item evidence (non-interactive planning run):

- Q: "Is the AC0 gate (>60 % local busy for a full night) met?" - Answer
  (evidence: `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI + `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`):
  **No.** 2.2 % busy for 2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00 (719 s of
  32 400 s, 27 streams, prefill 336 slot-s, decode 383 slot-s); 10.2 % for the
  24 h window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52. Source: CLI run recorded in
  the pre-check comment (`/tmp/wl-gate-check`).
- Q: "Has micro-batch tuning already been attempted, and with what result?"
  - Answer (evidence: LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS, `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md`):
  yes - ubatch 1024 -> 2048 gave 1.04x at p90 over 20k+ batches and was
  reverted; the close-out rule is to re-measure at 40-80k tokens. The plan
  therefore spends one child on the 40-80k measurement capability first.
- Q: "Are the prefill-related proxy knobs still available to tune?" - Answer
  (evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` + LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D): no - budget
  25 000 tokens, deadline 120 s, p75 pricing from 20k tokens and safety
  fraction 0.95 are already live. The plan re-validates their pricing after
  the launch-flag change instead of re-tuning them blind.

Open questions for the producer:

- **OPEN QUESTION** (geometry authority, directed to the producer): should the
  geometry prerequisite be LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN (*1 slot @262K vs 2 slots
  @131K*) - the experiment this item names - or LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5
  (*snapshot pool 2 -> 4 instead of more live slots*)? It matters because the
  winning geometry bounds the largest prompt the 40-80k harness can send and
  changes the micro-batch interaction. **Recommended:** keep
  LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN authoritative and treat LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5 as a
  parallel, independently decided item.
- **OPEN QUESTION** (gate window definition, directed to the producer): is
  "a full night" the wall-clock night used here (22:00-07:00) or the configured
  cheap window (01:00-10:00, `server.priority_window`)? **Recommended:**
  22:00-07:00, as written in AC0, with the busy % taken from the
  `definition: dispatch_to_finish` upper bound.

Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 04:20 UTC - plan session: pre-check deviation recorded, gate
  evidence captured (NOT met), duplicate-work check against 5 keywords, 9
  children created in test-first order, 20 dependency edges wired (all children
  gated on LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ; batch work additionally gated on LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN), effort/risk
  re-estimated (Medium/Medium, 51.22 h recommended), six review stages run, AC
  coverage verified.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a measured comparison of **1 llama-server slot with
262,144 ctx** versus **2 slots with 131,072 ctx each**, so we can choose the
geometry that maximises local work served without unacceptable queueing.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This experiment can only be carried out when we have a full night of GPU use
(>60% busy).** With local currently at ~10% busy, a 1-vs-2 slot comparison
measures noise, not saturation: the trade-off only shows up when demand
actually contends for slots. Verify the gate with the
`proxy-usage-analysis` report's `## Local model utilization` section for a
complete night window: busy must be >= 60% for the full night. Record that
evidence in a comment on this item before starting; if the gate is not met,
leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Current geometry: `--parallel 2` with `--ctx-size 262144` = **131,072 tokens
  per slot**.
- Measured concurrency: **avg 1.04 while busy, peak 2** — demand is nearly
  serial today, so 2 slots are rarely both used.
- The routing hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 120000`)
  sits just under the 131K per-slot limit. In the 24h window **2,064 requests
  were skipped as `context_too_large`** (estimated > 120K), including 105
  skips from sessions that were already warm (cache ratio 0.92-1.00, only ~4K
  new tokens, total 126K-137K). A single 262K slot would move that ceiling
  from ~120K to ~258K.
- Local was idle **89.8%** of the window, serving only 225 turns across 26
  sessions, so spare capacity is not the current constraint — but slot
  geometry determines what will be servable once demand is raised.

## Hypothesis to test

- **1 x 262K**: ~2x per-slot context → far fewer `context_too_large` skips and
  larger conversations stay local; cost: requests serialise when two sessions
  overlap (today: peak 2, avg 1.04, so the cost may be small).
- **2 x 131K**: current state; parallel but capped at ~120K per request; the
  evidence above shows warm sessions being cut off at the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment records the measured >60% GPU busy for a full night
  from the usage-analysis report, before any configuration change.
- AC1: A repeatable measurement protocol is defined and written on this item:
  identical workload window length, same metrics, same report tooling for both
  arms.
- AC2: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a
  comparable period at the gate, with llama-server `--parallel` / `--ctx-size`
  changed together (and `session_slot_pool_size` plus the warm/cold thresholds
  adjusted consistently, since per-slot ctx and slot count interact — see
  LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP on the band collapsing to zero
  width).
- AC3: Results compare, for each arm: local busy %, turns served locally,
  requests diverted per fallback reason (especially `context_too_large` and

  first token, prefill and decode phase slot-seconds, and any errors

- AC4: A decision is recorded on this item: keep 2 slots, move to 1 slot, or
  make it mode-dependent, with the data that justifies it. If 1 slot wins, the
  follow-on config change is filed (or implemented if in scope).
- AC5: Findings feed the configuration documentation (`models.ini` launch
  flags, `proxy/config.yaml` slot/ctx comments) and the usage-analysis skill's
  interpretation section if the guidance changes
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`), plus any log-consuming
  script that assumes a fixed slot count or per-slot ctx.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill for any config/code change made.

## Notes

- Depends on demand having been raised first (thresholds / serve-first
  admission); that is why the >60% busy gate exists.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (local ctx-size evaluation), and the
  prefill-latency optimisation item — decide geometry before micro-tuning.

Sequenced features in dependency order (execution order for `wl next`):

2. **Geometry A/B protocol and reporter** (LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP) — `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` (protocol, window, metrics, pre-registered gate), `scripts/slot_geometry_ab_report.py` + fixture tests, `scripts/slot_geometry_arm.py` apply/verify helper. Test-first; can start while the gate is unmet.

5. **Arm comparison and geometry decision** (LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY) — blocked by 4; applies the pre-registered gate, records verdict + follow-on item.
6. **Propagate geometry decision to docs** (LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7) — blocked by 5; models.ini / config.yaml comments, usage-analysis REFERENCE, log-consumer audit.
7. **Suite green and geometry assertions** (LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP) — blocked by 6; `/skill:test` green + slot/ctx alignment assertions.

Reuse: env plumbing already exists (`LLAMA_PARALLEL`, `LLAMA_CTX_SIZE` in start-llama.sh; `session_slot_pool_size` drives it); per-slot clamp/band logic is in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` with existing unit coverage; usage-analysis report already emits busy/prefill/decode metrics. Precedent harness: `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py`.

Pre-registered decision-gate defaults (proposal — confirm at implement time unless overridden by the producer): adopt **1 x 262K** when, relative to Arm A, (a) turns served locally does not decrease, (b) `context_too_large` + `large_context_bypass` diverts fall by >= 50 %, (c) p90 dispatch→first-byte does not worsen by > 30 %, (d) local busy % does not regress by > 10 points; otherwise keep 2 slots (or choose mode-dependent with the recorded numbers).

Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: raise the economic ceiling ratio so warm = clamp (258,048), cold unchanged (38,000), band non-collapsed (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP). Rationale: leaving it at 120K means the extra slot context is never routed to, defeating the arm. Final confirmation delegated to implement time unless the producer overrides.

## Goal

Evaluate (with measurements, go/no-go) whether widening the **per-session KV snapshot pool** (`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4, snapshots under `session_slot_save_path/slot_<id>.bin`) raises local prefix reuse for the small/medium working set — as the recommended alternative to adding live llama slots, which would shrink per-slot context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots) and exclude the long-context sessions that dominate this workload.

## Why

- Measured prefix reuse is poor: aggregate 26.1 %, median **15.6 %** for prompts >20k tokens (227 prompts), 28 fully cold; 27 distinct sessions cycled through a 2-slot pool in ~5.4 h.
- More live slots buy *residency*, not throughput (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills), and cost per-slot address space for a long-context workload.
- The snapshot mechanism already exists (per-session save/restore, `session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds: 0.0015`, capped at `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds: 60`, pool capped by `session_slot_pool_size: 2`) but is degraded under load (`session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`, circuit-breaker cooldown). Restore cost estimate: ~50k tokens ≈ 75 s → capped 60 s, so the mechanism currently helps only the <40k band.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Benchmark:** measure save/restore latency (and disk footprint) per prompt-size band (10k / 25k / 40k / 60k+) on the production GPU host, including under load (another session streaming), against the 0.0015 s/token timeout model.
- **AC2 — Go/no-go with evidence:** with `session_slot_pool_size: 4` in a replay/bake-off on the 2026-10-24 thrash window (or equivalent fixture), report the reuse uplift (baseline 15.6 % median for >20k prompts) and the restore-success rate (skip_when_busy / cooldown exclusions).
- **AC3 — If go:** ship the config change plus retention/eviction semantics for 4 snapshots (pool eviction policy, disk cap, failure cooldowns unchanged) and any report/observability fields (restore-hit rate per session, snapshot pool occupancy) so the proxy-usage-analysis report can monitor the effect.
- **AC4 — If no-go:** record the measured blockers (latency, skip rate, restore failures) as a comment on this item so the decision is reproducible.
- **AC5 — No change to live slot count or per-slot ctx in this item** (that remains the separate 3-slot "fast" profile discussion).

## Tests

Bake-off harness replaying fixture logs + real save/restore micro-benchmark on the host; unit tests for pool-size > 2 retention semantics; report-schema tests for the new fields.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (slot-churn / tenancy investigation, option 3a of the recommendation).
- This is an evaluation/deliberation item, not a mandate to change configuration.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD** – Slot-count benchmark: find optimal session_slot_pool_size for Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MPOL5S7W007GRWB** – Include router model in slot save/restore requests (completed)
- **LP-0MU03AL730000B5W** – Slot counts: default and fast -> 1 slot, cheap -> 3 slots (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: 10k, 50k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+134 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: 10k, 50k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+134 more)
