## Objective

Execute the **24 h post-deploy verification of AC4** for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`
(resident-prefix admission + session tenancy) on a restart-free production
window and record whether **scheduling-attributed** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
cancellations fell by **≥ 90 %** against that same window's own re-anchored
baseline — plus the AC5 observability and AC6 lease-watchdog checks.

This item only measures and reports; it changes no scheduling logic.

## Problem statement

The epic's AC4 cannot be verified inside the implementing session: it needs a
full 24 h production soak on code that is actually running. Verification also
silently invalidates itself — the proxy restarted **six times on 2026-10-25**
(log rotations at 11:01:54, 11:21:20, 11:46:48, 18:57:27, 20:16:58 and
21:18:04 UTC), and each restart resets the in-memory residency/lease state, so
a window that contains a restart measures nothing. Without a pinned window,
attested uptime, and a window-scoped baseline, the ≥ 90 % claim is
unfalsifiable.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — needs a defensible verdict on the thrash change before
  the epic closes, and needs to know whether to roll back.
  - *As the proxy operator, I want the 24 h result stated with its window,
    counts and baseline, so I can accept the change or roll it back.*
- **Implementing agents of the epic** — need AC4 satisfied by an independent
  measurement, not by their own in-session numbers.
  - *As the epic's implementing agent, I want the verdict recorded on the epic,
    so I can close AC4 without self-certifying.*
- **Future thrash investigations** — need the measured window, the corrected
  commands and the classifier rule as precedent.
  - *As a future investigator, I want the procedure and its numbers in
    `findings.md`, so I do not re-derive the methodology.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Preconditions attested before measuring.** The result records: the
  proxy PID and its start instant (`ps -o lstart -p <pid>`), continuous uptime
  covering the entire window, the code identity read **from the checkout the
  running proxy was started from** (`git log -1 --format=%H` — the checkout is
  shared, so the tip moves without a restart), and explicit confirmation that
  both target changes are in that tree (`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` ladder;
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` 25k cold budget / 120 s deadline).
- **AC2 — Window pinned and restart-free.** The window is
  `2026-10-26T21:02:00Z → 2026-10-27T21:02:00Z` (ISO-8601 UTC, exactly 24 h,
  start ≥ the latest proxy restart), pinned in this description before the run
  (Q1 decision A: no cron alignment).
  Restart-freedom is evidenced by `ps -o lstart` plus the absence of
  `Logging initialised … pid=` / `Rotated previous proxy log aside` lines
  between start and end. A restart inside the window re-arms the run (new
  window, both windows recorded) and never yields a PASS.
- **AC3 — Absolute counts recorded.** `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events and
  total wasted prefill tokens for the window, with the
  `LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM` caveat stated (event fields are recomputed post-hoc, so
  `wasted_prefill_tokens` is overstated; the figure is either re-derived from
  admission-side data or reported with that caveat).
- **AC4 — Scheduling-attributed split, reproducible.** Every deadline event is
  classified as scheduling-attributed when either (a) the `reuse_ratio` logged
  at admission was below `server.local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`
  (0.5 in `proxy/config.yaml`), or (b) `slot_owner_session` at admission
  differs from the owner at the deadline event. Per-class counts are recorded;
  the remainder is reported as genuine GPU-speed misses and declared out of
  scope. Because the event line logs only `session` and `deadline`
  (`proxy/proxy/router.py` ~line 1616), the classifier joins each event to the
  session's most recent `routing_resident_prefix` line and any `local_eviction*`
  line before it — the join rule is stated in the result, and events whose
  join is ambiguous are counted separately and **not** as scheduling-attributed
  (conservative).
- **AC5 — Baseline re-anchored to the same window.** Baseline is computed by
  capturing the window with `capture_prefill_thrash_window.py` and replaying it
  through the residency ladder with `replay_prefill_occupancy.py
  --window-fixture`, and the reduction percentage against the
  scheduling-attributed count is stated explicitly. The 2026-10-24 figures
  (160 events / 5.4 h ≈ 780k wasted prefill tokens) are historical reference
  only and are never the baseline.
- **AC6 — Verdict recorded with both gates.** **PASS** requires (i) ≥ 90 %
  reduction in scheduling-attributed cancellations and (ii) no
  `local_lease_active` refusal window longer than the 180 s watchdog bound. On
  FAIL the measured numbers are recorded, a `discovered-from` item is created
  with the offending log extract, and this item is not marked complete.
- **AC7 — Staged-rollout observability check.** The window's
  `analyze_proxy_usage.py` report contains `## Residency-aware admission` with
  the `residency_decisions` / `residency_resident_admits` /
  `residency_evicted_denials` / `residency_tenant_limit_denials` /
  `local_evictions` counters and the per-session slot-owner churn table. An
  absent section, or decisions logged but all unmeasured, is a finding (ladder
  not emitting), never a pass.
- **AC8 — Result recorded and propagated.** One structured result comment on
  this item (window bounds, precondition attestation, counts, classified split,
  baseline, reduction %, verdict), cross-referenced from
  `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and from
  `Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)`,
  which consumes the same report set (Q2 decision A) rather than running its
  own window.
- **AC9 — Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`
  gains the measured window and verdict (and the corrected capture invocation
  with `--log`), so the 2026-10-24 numbers are labelled historical; all related
  documentation (code comments, README, docs site entries) is updated to
  reflect the changes.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (executed
  via the test skill / dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs).

## Constraints

- **No restart inside the window.** Evidence that this is the dominant risk:
  six restarts on 2026-10-25 alone; the 21:18:10 restart was
  `source=manual actor=unknown`. A restart resets residency/lease state and
  invalidates the run.
- **Do not run before the pinned instant, and do not peek early** in a way that
  biases the decision.
- **Read-only measurement:** no `start-proxy.sh --restart`, no config reload, no
  log truncation during the window. Rotated logs (`.gz`) are part of the
  window and must be passed to the capture tool.
- **Counters come from the analysis tool**, not ad-hoc `grep`
  (`LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G` exposes first-class `--json` keys); `grep` is only used
  for the classification join and for spot evidence.
- **Baseline is window-scoped**, per AC5.
- Analysis window is given with explicit `--start`/`--end` (the
  `05:00 UTC`-boundary convention is a convenience, not a requirement of the
  tool — see Decisions (Q1).

## Existing state (evidence gathered 2026-10-25T23:20–23:35Z)

- **Latest proxy restart: 2026-10-25T21:18:10Z**, PID **3057415**
  (`ps -o lstart -p 3057415` → `Sun Oct 25 21:18:08 2026`; log head:
  `Logging initialised at /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log pid=3057415`
  followed by `Proxy restart attribution: source=manual actor=unknown`).
  ⇒ earliest legal run instant is **2026-10-27T21:02Z**; the item's previous
  instant (11:22Z) is stale.
- **Ladder is emitting:** 871 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions since the
  21:18:10 restart; corrected form present
  (`n_past_actual=none … reuse_ratio=none … residency_source=non_resident`).
- **23 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events** since the restart (~2 h), all
  `deadline=120s`, e.g. `session=audit-SA-0MVO7XZAB0095R6F-phase2_deep-…` —
  audit sessions visibly dominate the sample, so the user/audit split matters.
- **Report section verified live** for 22:18–23:18: `## Residency-aware
  admission` renders — 446 residency decisions (0 measured / 446 unmeasured),
  9 `tenant_limit` denials, 16 `local_eviction` (8 `local_eviction_after_acceptance`,
  all `prefill_deadline`), 4 of 23 sessions with slot-owner churn.
- **Pipeline smoke-tested end to end** (22:30–23:00): capture → 430 attempts,
  1 deadline-cancelled, ~2152 wasted tokens modelled; replay → 421 over budget,
  9 admitted, **0 over-budget cold admissions**.
- **Gap found — the documented capture command is incomplete:** the item's
  re-anchoring snippet omits `--log`, which is required
  (`capture_prefill_thrash_window.py: error: the following arguments are
  required: --log`). Corrected form is used in this brief.
- **Gap found — classification needs a join:** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
  logs only `session` + `deadline`, so rule (b) cannot be read off the event
  line itself; it must be joined per session (see AC4).
- **`local_lease_active` is observable**: 37 occurrences since the restart
  (e.g. `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue … queued_duration=60.00s
  reason=local_lease_active`), so the AC6 watchdog check is measurable.
- **Overlapping verification item exists:** `LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` (Post-deploy
  24 h prefill regression verification, `plan_complete`, promoted to top level
  on 2026-10-25T22:23Z) measures the same change set with a different window
  (2026-10-25T20:17Z → 2026-10-26T20:17Z, code `fc3c6e2e`) and the historical
  fixture-restated baseline rather than a window-scoped re-anchoring. **That
  window is now invalid:** the 21:18:10 restart falls inside it. Two
  independent runs would produce two contradictory verdicts — see Open
  Question 2.
- **Armed origin:** this item was created and retitled by
  `LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P` (`completed`), whose AC4 (deliverable) requires this
  item to carry the deploy-derived instant, the pinned window, the
  re-anchoring query and the classifier.

## Desired change

Nothing in the scheduling path. This item produces:

1. A pinned, restart-free 24 h window recorded on the item **before** the run.
2. One measurement run of the usage analysis plus the re-anchored baseline
   replay, with the scheduling-attributed split applied.
3. A structured result comment with the PASS/FAIL verdict, propagated to the
   epic (and to `LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` if it shares this run).
4. The corresponding `findings.md` entry, so the methodology and the numbers
   are reusable.

## Measurement commands (verified working 2026-10-25)

```bash
# 0. Preconditions (attest before measuring, AC1/AC2)
ps -o pid,lstart -p $(pgrep -f "uvicorn proxy.server:app" | head -1)
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm && git log -1 --format='%H %ci'

# 1. Window report (AC3, AC6, AC7) — explicit window, first-class counters
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
  --start "2026-10-26 21:02:00" --end "2026-10-27 21:02:00" \
  --output-dir ~/proxy-usage-reports/ac4 --json

# 2. Window-scoped baseline (AC5) — every log file overlapping the window,
#    incl. in-process rotations (proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS) and .gz
python3 proxy/scripts/capture_prefill_thrash_window.py \
  --start "2026-10-26 21:02:00" --end "2026-10-27 21:02:00" \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-26_* \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log-2026-10-26_00 \
  --out /tmp/ac4_window.jsonl
python3 proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py x \
  --window-fixture /tmp/ac4_window.jsonl    # expects 0 over-budget cold admissions

# 3. Classifier join (AC4) — per-session decision before each deadline event
grep -E "prefill_deadline_exceeded|routing_resident_prefix|local_eviction" \
  /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
```

## Pinned measurement window (Q1 — operator decision A, 2026-10-25)

- **Start:** `2026-10-25T21:19:00Z` (**already elapsed** — the binding
  restart-anchored freeze is therefore in effect immediately).
- **End / run instant:** `2026-10-26T21:19:00Z` — the analysis runs at/after
  this instant and covers the full 24 h.
- No cron/05:00 alignment (dropped by decision; `analyze_proxy_usage.py`
  takes explicit `--start`/`--end`).
- **Re-arm rule (binding, unchanged):** any proxy restart between now and
  `2026-10-27T21:02Z` invalidates this window; retitle this item to
  `latest_restart + 24 h` and re-pin before running. A restart **after**
  `start` has already been open for 2+ h wastes that elapsed time, so the
  freeze announcement applies immediately.

## Shared measurement (Q2 — operator decision A, 2026-10-25)

`Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification
(LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)` (**re-based by comment 2026-10-25**) consumes this
run's report for its waste/503/eviction-reason/rollback checks instead of
running a separate window. This item owns the scheduling-attributed
classifier, the window-scoped re-anchored baseline, AC5 observability and the
AC6 watchdog check. Exactly one report set is produced and reused.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — window
  report + `--json` counters for AC3, AC6, AC7.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — renders
  `## Residency-aware admission` (AC7).
- `proxy/scripts/capture_prefill_thrash_window.py` — window capture; requires
  `--start/--end/--log/--out` (AC5).
- `proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py` — `--window-fixture` replay
  through the real ladder (AC5).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `prefill_deadline_exceeded` logging (~line 1616);
  the join key for AC4, no change expected.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0.5`, cold budget
  25 000, prefill deadline 120 s (AC4, AC6 thresholds).
- `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md` — destination for the
  result (AC9).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — restart inside the window (highest).** Six restarts on 2026-10-25,
  several from concurrent agent sessions. Mitigation: pin the window, re-arm on
  restart, and announce the freeze on in-flight proxy items; never silently
  re-run with a partially-reset window.
- **Risk — ambiguous classifier joins.** A session may log many residency
  decisions before its deadline event. Mitigation: use the latest decision
  before the event, publish the rule, count ambiguous events separately
  (conservative, out of the scheduling-attributed numerator).
- **Risk — waste figure overstated** (`LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM`). Mitigation:
  report with the caveat or re-derive from admission-side data.
- **Risk — audit traffic dominates** deadline events. Mitigation: report the
  user/audit split (matches `LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` AC2(a)).
- **Risk — log rotation inside the window** hides events in `.gz`. Mitigation:
  pass every rotated file (and `.gz`) to the capture tool.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the missing event-line fields (AC4 join) may justify a
  small logging-enrichment item. That is a **linked work item**, not scope
  here.
- **Assumption:** dev code runs live on this server, so the deploy instant is
  the proxy restart (operator-confirmed 2026-10-25, recorded by
  `LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P`).
- **Assumption:** `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` remains `0.5` for the
  window; it is read from `proxy/config.yaml` at measurement time and recorded.

## Related work

- Local slot scheduling: session-level tenancy and resident-prefix admission
  (stop cold-prefill thrash in 2 slots) (`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`) — epic;
  AC4/AC5/AC6 are satisfied only by this item's result.
- Cold-prefill admission budget 25k tokens + prefill deadline 90s -> 120s, with
  post-acceptance eviction logged as ERROR (`LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`) — its deploy
  is part of the clock (now live).
- [chore] Staged rollout and AC4 follow-up arming (`LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P`) —
  armed this item (retitle, pinned window, re-anchoring query, classifier).
- Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification (`LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I`) —
  overlapping 24 h verification — shared measurement per Q2 decision A
  (window re-based to this item's by comment 2026-10-25).
- Residual 120 s deadline evictions with zero prefill progress: second-slot
  head-of-line blocking (warm prompts) (`LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I`) — its class is
  reported separately, not counted as a failure here.
- AC7 eviction event reports recomputed new_tokens/ETA, not the admission
  decision's values (false over-budget signal) (`LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM`) — waste
  overstatement caveat.
- Expose prefill-regression metrics (deadline events, budget refusals, wasted
  tokens, provider exhaustion, 503s) in proxy-usage-analysis
  (`LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G`) — first-class `--json` counters used for AC3/AC7.
- Cold-prefill thrash-window regression fixture harness

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the parent item's gating precondition verified from
measured evidence, so that prefill tuning only starts once local actually
carries sustained work.

## What the gate is

Parent **LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT** AC0 requires a comment recording a measured
**>60 % local (GPU) busy** night before any change is made. Busy is the
`## Local model utilization` upper bound (dispatch -> finish: prefill +
decode) from the deterministic `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI, over a complete
night window (22:00-07:00 local).

## Evidence at planning time (2026-10-25)

- Night **2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00**: busy **2.2 %** (719 s of
  32 400 s; 27 local streams; prefill 336 slot-s; decode 383 slot-s;
  idle 97.8 %).
  Command:
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-23 22:00:00" --end "2026-10-24 07:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/wl-gate-check --json`
- Same night in the 24 h daily report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`,
  window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52): busy 10.2 %.

**The gate is NOT met.** The parent is left `blocked` at stage
`plan_complete`, and every other child of this plan depends on this item, so
none of them is dispatchable until the gate passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0: The gate AC is satisfied - a comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation for a full night, from the usage-analysis report, before any change is made.
- AC1: A comment on the parent records local busy % for a **complete** night
  window (22:00-07:00), with the exact CLI invocation, the window bounds and
  the artifact directory used.
- AC2: The gate is declared met **only** when `busy_pct >= 60` for the whole
  night (`definition: dispatch_to_finish` in the CLI `--json` summary).
- AC3: When the gate is not met this item stays **open and incomplete** with
  the evidence comment (recorded `blocked` status is derived from dependency
  edges in `wl` and cannot be pinned, so this item is the lock: keeping it
  incomplete keeps every dependent child dependency-blocked), and no other
  child of the plan is started.
- AC6: This item must never be marked `completed` while the gate is unmet. If a
  run cannot leave it open, it records the evidence and files the deferral on
  the parent rather than completing the gate.
- AC4: When the gate is met this item completes with the evidence comment and
  the parent plus its dependent siblings are unblocked in the same update
  sequence.
- AC5: Measurement only - no configuration, flag or code change.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` - deterministic report CLI
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report section definitions

## Dependencies

None. All other children of this plan depend on this item.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the A/B benchmark harness to produce valid measurements
in the **40-80k-token** band, because that is the band that produces the
multi-minute local first-byte tail and the only band in which a micro-batch
change can still help.

## Why

`docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS) measured 8.9k / 17.9k
/ 26.8k prompts, found the ubatch 1024->2048 win confined to ~18k (memory
bandwidth bound above), and closed with: *"If this is revisited: measure at
40k-80k tokens"*. The parent item is that revisit, so the harness must be
trustworthy at that size first. Today `build_prompt()` targets ~4 chars/token
without reporting llama-server's real `prompt_tokens`, `--sizes` is free-form,
and a single 80k prefill can take minutes under GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The harness records llama-server's reported `prompt_tokens` per sample
  and fails loudly when the delivered size deviates from the requested size by
  more than 10 %, so a mis-sized prompt cannot silently invalidate a bin.
- AC2: An end-to-end run at `--sizes 40960,61440,81920 --reps 3` produces a
  JSON result with per-size p50/p90 and the 20k+ headline aggregate within a
  documented time budget and timeout.
- AC3: Offline unit tests cover prompt sizing/token accounting, percentile
  aggregation, size-deviation rejection and argument validation - no live
  server required.
- AC4: `docs/dev/` records the band methodology and validity guards: unique
  prompt text per repetition, `cache_prompt: false`, the TTS/GPU-contention
  noise rule, and minimum reps.
- AC5: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - the A/B harness
- `tests/test_ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - offline harness tests
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior experiment record to extend

## Implementation sketch (test-first)

1. Extend the offline tests for the new validations.
2. Report and validate actual `prompt_tokens`; fail fast on a mis-sized bin.
3. Add a documented default band (`40960,61440,81920`) and a per-size timeout
   policy.
4. Record the methodology in `docs/dev/`.

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) -
  a 40-80k prompt must fit the per-slot context.

## Out of scope

Changing llama-server flags, routing or admission policy.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want `--ubatch-size` and `--batch-size` re-measured in the
40-80k band against a pre-registered win threshold, so the values shipped in
`models.ini` are justified by measurement rather than inherited.

## Context

- Current `[Qwen3]` launch flags: `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2
  --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024 --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0
  --cache-type-v q8_0 --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`,
  plus `flash-attn`.
- Prior A/B (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS, `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md`): 1.04x
  at p90 over 20k+ batches, reverted. Its close-out rule is that a retry must
  be measured at 40-80k.
- Geometry interacts: per-slot context (`--ctx-size / --parallel`) bounds the
  largest prompt the harness can send, so this item starts only after the
  geometry experiment has recorded its decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch configuration, each changed value justified by measurement rather than guesswork, or reverted and recorded.
- AC1: A hypothesis and numeric decision gate are written on this item BEFORE
  the first measurement (for example: adopt when p90 prompt-eval tok/s improves
  by >= 1.3x in the 60-80k bins with decode regression <= 2 %).
- AC2: Candidate values (`--ubatch-size` 2048 and 4096; `--batch-size` 8192 vs
  16384) are measured one variable at a time on arm-identical workloads with
  >= 3 reps using the 40-80k band harness; raw JSON is archived under
  `benchmark-results/`.
- AC3: Each knob gets an explicit adopt/revert decision with measured numbers;
  an adopted value is written to `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with the measurement
  and rollback value in the comment, a rejected value is recorded as reverted
  to 1024 / 8192.
- AC4: VRAM and stability are checked per arm (clean llama-server start, no
  OOM, `rocm-smi` within budget); the restart that empties the 40 GiB prompt
  cache is recorded so proxy first-byte stats are not compared across it.
- AC5: Any test or script asserting the flags is updated in the same change and
  the full suite is green via the test skill.
- AC6: If no value wins, the item completes with a recorded NO-GO and the
  parent's tuning scope narrows to the proxy-knob/ETA-guard half.

**Key Files:**
- `./models.ini` - `[Qwen3]` launch flags
- `./start-llama.sh` - flag defaults passed to llama-server
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - measurement harness
- `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh` - flag assertions
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior record to extend
- `benchmark-results/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22-candidate-2048.json` - prior raw arm data

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Baseline prefill measurement capture.
- 40-80k prefill benchmark capability.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN).

## Out of scope

`--cache-ram`, KV-cache quantisation, ctx-size/slot geometry, `--threads`,
`--mlock` and `--swa-checkpoints` (see the sibling launch-flag item).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard and the prefill
deadline re-checked against the post-change prefill rates and the interaction
documented, so a faster GPU cannot silently make the budget/deadline wrong.

## Context

- Live knobs - deployed by LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D, do **not** re-tune without new
  evidence: `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`,
  `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction: 0.95`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile: 75`,
  `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 600`.
- The guard calibrates itself from a rolling window of per-dispatch samples
  `(coded_tokens, new_tokens, dispatch_to_first_byte_ms)` keyed by
  `(model, context bucket)`, so it re-calibrates automatically. But the budget
  (25k) and deadline (120 s) were derived from the OLD band rates (249 t/s at
  20-30k, 114 t/s at 63k). If prefill becomes materially faster, both may be
  re-derivable - a decision for measurement, not guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the configuration (llama-server launch flags and the prefill-related proxy knobs) where measurement justifies each change, otherwise left unchanged and recorded.
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's configuration and documentation are updated together, and the local_prefill_deadline_seconds / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC1: Matched before/after windows compare guard behaviour: admit vs reject
  counts by reason (`prefill_budget_exceeded`, `eta_exceeds_budget`,
  `prefill_deadline_exceeded`), thrash-cooldown events and cancelled prefills.
- AC2: The measured band rates (10-20k, 20-30k, 30-40k, 40-60k, 60-80k) are
  re-derived from the post-change window and compared numerically with the
  rates the budget and deadline were derived from.
- AC3: A decision is recorded on whether 25 000 tokens / 120 s remain optimal;
  any change is justified by AC1/AC2 numbers, shipped in one change with its
  config comment, and carries a documented rollback.
- AC4: The `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` <-> ETA-guard <->
  contention-queue interaction (the ordering invariant
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds < local_prefill_deadline_seconds <
  local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`)
  is documented in one authoritative place (config comments plus a `docs/dev/`
  note) and the tests asserting the ordering still pass.
- AC5: Guard/calibration code is unchanged unless a measured defect is found;
  if changed, unit tests cover the new behaviour.
- AC6: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` - calibration and admission guard
- `proxy/config.yaml` - guard, budget and deadline configuration
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta.py` - calibration tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` - conservative pricing tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` - deadline interaction tests
- `docs/dev/prefill-eta-deadline-interaction.md` - authoritative interaction note

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Baseline prefill measurement capture.
- Launch-flag A/B: ubatch and batch size (the rates it changes).
- Launch-flag A/B: threads and SWA checkpoints.

## Out of scope

Re-litigating the values shipped by LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D without new
post-change evidence.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the >60 % local-busy precondition measured and recorded on
the parent (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) **before** any geometry change, so the 1-vs-2
slot comparison is run against a contended GPU window instead of idle noise.

## Context

The parent's GATING PRECONDITION: local is currently ~10 % busy, so a 1-vs-2 slot
comparison would measure noise. The trade-off (overlapping sessions serialising
behind one slot) only appears when demand actually contends for slots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `proxy-usage-analysis` report is generated for a complete night window and its `## Local model utilization` section shows busy >= 60 % for that full window.
- AC2: The evidence (report path, window start/end, busy %, turns served, session count) is recorded as a comment on LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN before any configuration change.
- AC3: If busy < 60 %, the parent is left blocked with the measured number recorded: no arm is run and no geometry flag is changed.
- AC4: The exact window (start, end, length in hours) is recorded so Arm A and Arm B can be given identical-length windows.

# Pin start-proxy.sh shell-level `--restart` preserve-vs-restart decision with a pytest test

## Problem statement

`start-proxy.sh --restart` decides whether to preserve a warm llama-server by
comparing the `config_sha256` recorded in `.llama_server_signature.json` with a
freshly computed `merged_config_sha256` of `proxy/config.yaml`; on a match it
preserves ("Preserving running llama-server (unchanged local backend config)."),
otherwise it kills and restarts llama-server. That shell branch is currently
the **only** untested consumer of the merged-config signature: the sole
coverage lives in `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, which
LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 deletes (mode-era harness). The Python tests cover the hash
helper and the signature writer (`proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`,
`proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`), not the shell decision that acts on
them — so a regression there (e.g. comparing the wrong path, ignoring the flag)
would go unnoticed and would either kill a warm llama-server on every restart
or silently preserve a stale one.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — the warm KV/prompt cache must survive a proxy-only
  restart, and a genuine local-backend change must restart llama-server.
- **Future implementation agents** — need the shell branch pinned so changes to
  `start-proxy.sh` restart handling fail loudly in the default suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Unchanged config preserves llama-server.** A pytest test runs a
  sandboxed copy of `start-proxy.sh --foreground --restart` whose signature
  file matches `merged_config_sha256(proxy/config.yaml, proxy/config.yaml)` and
  asserts the "Preserving running llama-server" line is emitted and the fake
  `pkill` log contains **no** `llama-server` kill.
- **AC2 — Changed config restarts llama-server.** With the sandbox config
  edited after the signature was written (merged hash changes), the preserving
  line is absent and the fake `pkill` log shows a `llama-server` kill.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe signatures.** Missing, empty or corrupt signature /
  unreadable hash → conservative restart (never an unearned preserve), asserted
  behaviourally.
- **AC4 — Explicit override still wins.** `--keep-llama-server` forces
  preservation even when the signature mismatches (flag beats hash).
- **AC5 — Sandbox isolation.** The test copies the script into a temp dir with
  stubbed `pkill`/`fuser`/`ss`/`netstat`, an isolated `$HOME`, an ephemeral port
  and a fake interpreter intercepting the final `exec uvicorn`; it never
  touches the live proxy, llama-server, TTS or ports 8000/8080/8081, and never
  issues a blanket kill. It is collected by the default pytest suite (unlike
  the bare `tests/*.sh` harnesses).
- **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.**
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No behaviour change to `start-proxy.sh`: this is coverage for the existing
  contract. A defect found while writing it becomes a separate work item.
- Reuse the established sandbox pattern in
  `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` (fake `python3` recording argv,
  stubbed process/port probes) rather than inventing a new harness.
- The signature schema is written by `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
  (`_write_llama_server_signature`: `mode`, `model`, `parallel`, `router_mode`,
  `config_sha256`); fixtures must match it.
- UK English.

## Existing state

- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (being deleted by LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29) holds
  the only behavioural assertions for this branch; after deletion the branch has
  none.
- `grep -rln "Preserving running llama-server"` matches only that harness and
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` asserts the flag is *documented*
  (`test_start_proxy_help_documents_keep_llama_server`) and pins the Python hash
  helper — not the shell preserve/restart decision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_signature.py` — new pytest test (name
  indicative).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` — sandbox pattern to reuse.
- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — script under test (read-only).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `merged_config_sha256` fixture hash.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — signature schema reference.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29** — deletes the stale mode-era harness; this item
  replaces the one piece of live coverage that deletion removes.
- **LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H**, **LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8** — duplicate items closed
  in favour of LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 (producer decision B).
- **LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW** — restart signature hashes the merged config.
- **LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN** — preserve-the-warm-llama-server design.

data.description:
## Observed behaviour (2026-10-25, UTC)

Session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` (`/skill:intake RISE-0MVLHZW7B003XEHV`) was pinned to local routing by its client (`X-Local-Preference: local-only`). The local admission guard refused it:

```
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=true
              priority=medium session=herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152
11:57:09,999  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=false  (same session)
```

Both refusals were answered with **HTTP 429 and `error: "All providers exhausted"`**:

- direct/lease path: `provider.py:10938` → `_build_exhausted_response()` → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` → `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`code: local_admission_reject`, `error: "All providers exhausted"`)
- contention-queue path: `provider.py:10334` / `:11291` → `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`error: "Local admission refused"`)

Remote providers were *available* throughout (`opencode-go` at 62 % effective headroom), so "All providers exhausted" is factually wrong, and the two paths disagree on the message for the same condition. The client (which retries on 429) backed off seven times and then reported the error as non-retryable; the user-visible symptom was "Error: 429 \"All providers exhausted\"".

## Goal

A local-only admission refusal is a *capacity/intent* outcome, not a chain exhaustion: it must be reported with one stable, distinguishable contract on every path, and "All providers exhausted" must be reserved for genuine chain exhaustion.

## Users

- **local-only clients** (herdr worker sessions) that must never be told the whole chain is dead when the local guard simply refused their oversized/over-budget prefill — the current prose makes them give up or retry blindly.
- **Client retry layers** that treat a truthful 429 as recoverable (`Retry-After` respects the per-reason timing from LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) instead of terminal.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both local-only refusal paths (direct/lease `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` guard, contention-queue/lease `refused_local_only`) return the same shape: HTTP 429, `Retry-After` (per-reason semantics per LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X), `X-Local-Route: refused`, the `X-Local-Admission*` headers, and a body whose `error` text does **not** contain "All providers exhausted".
2. The body carries a stable `code` distinct from `all_exhausted`, `outside_time_window` and `all_slots_exhausted` — the retained value is `local_admission_reject` (Appendix Q2) — and the human-readable `detail` states that the request was pinned local-only and the local guard refused it.
3. Genuine chain exhaustion is unchanged: `code: all_exhausted` / `outside_time_window` / `all_slots_exhausted` and the existing prose remain byte-compatible for older clients.
4. `prefer-local` fallthrough behaviour is unchanged: a guard refusal with `prefer-local` still routes to the next provider and never returns the refusal response.
5. `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the refusal codes, the "local-only" semantics and the client-side action (compact/retry/allow remote).
6. Tests: unit coverage for both refusal paths asserting status, `code`, `error` text and headers; a regression test asserting a real chain exhaustion still returns the exhaustion codes; a test asserting a local-only refusal *while remotes are available* never uses the exhaustion prose.

## Constraints

- Older clients depend on the existing exhaustion `code` values and prose — AC3 is byte-compatibility for `all_exhausted`/`outside_time_window`/`all_slots_exhausted` only.
- The refusal `error` string is parsed by at least one client retry loop (the operator-reported "Error: 429 \"All providers exhausted\""); the new text must be stable and greppable.
- `X-Local-Route: refused` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` are already emitted by `_stamp_local_route_headers()`/`_note_local_fallback_reason()` — the fix reuses these, it does not add a parallel routing signal.
- Retry timing is owned by child LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X; this brief keeps the header contract and defers per-reason `Retry-After` values to that item.

## Existing state

- Direct/lease local-only refusal funnels through `_build_exhausted_response()` (`provider.py:5583`) → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` (`:6508`) → `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`:5521`), which hard-codes `error: "All providers exhausted"` and a detail claiming "no remote provider is available" — false when remotes are up.
- Queue/lease `refused_local_only` returns `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`:6310`) with `error: "Local admission refused"` — the correct prose, but a different builder with a slightly different body/headers (no `retryable`, no token headers yet).
- Both builders already return 429 + `X-Local-Route: refused` + `X-Local-Admission*` (Eta/Budget) headers + `code: local_admission_reject` (`EXHAUSTION_CODE_LOCAL_ADMISSION`, `:5518`).

## Desired change

- Direct/lease path: stop routing the local-only refusal through the exhaustion builder — return the local-only refusal response directly (same builder as the queue path) so both paths share one shape and truthful prose.
- Reserve `_build_exhausted_response()` and `error: "All providers exhausted"` for genuine chain exhaustion (unchanged codes/prose).
- Keep `prefer-local` fallthrough untouched (AC4).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`:5521`), `_build_exhausted_response()` (`:5583`), `_local_admission_reject_payload()` (`:6508`), `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`:6310`), direct local-only branch (`:10938`), queue `refused_local_only` branches (`:10311`, `:11270`), `_request_local_preference()` (`:6305`), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (`:6387`).
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_error_code.py` — both-refusal-path unit coverage + chain-exhaustion regression + "remotes available" test.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `X-Local-Preference` semantics (`:1158`), `X-Local-Route` values (`:1173`), exhaustion/refusal contract; AC5 doc update lands here.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL — introduced `X-Local-Preference` + the AC4 refusal mechanics (completed; source of `X-Local-Route` and the `local_admission_reject` code value).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (completed; source of the refusal `code`).
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 — cold-prefill budget enforcement (completed; `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`).
- LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G — stable exhaustion codes (completed; AC3's byte-compat contract).
- LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X — truthful, reason-specific retry time (discovered-from this item; `intake_complete`, blocked on U2).
- LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG — local-only enforced on every skip path (discovered-from this item; `intake_complete`).
- LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ — local-only refusal invisible in proxy logs / false fallback line (open; related log-side defect).

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: changing the refusal `error`/`detail` text breaks a client that string-matches "All providers exhausted" on the refusal path. Mitigation: prose change is the point of the bug; keep `code` stable so machine clients are unaffected (AC2/AC3).
- Risk: unifies body shape but adds fields faster than clients adopt them. Mitigation: additive body fields only; `error`/`code`/`Retry-After` stay compatible with the older shape.
- Assumption: the two refusal paths should share the queue path's builder (`_build_local_only_refusal_response`) as the single source of truth.
- Scope-creep guard: enforcement on non-admission skip paths (U2), per-reason retry timing (T8), and admission-budget tuning are separate items — not this brief's scope.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (structure — resolved): the coverage review returned `stop` because the two children do **not** decompose this bug's six ACs — they are separate defects (skip-path enforcement, retry timing). Options were: (a) detach both children, making them independent items linked via `discovered-from:` so this bug closes on its own six ACs; (b) keep them as children and treat this item as an umbrella; (c) rework the children to absorb AC1–AC3. **Recommended:** (a) — this is a self-contained bug whose ACs need direct implementation, not a delegation epic. — Answer (producer, 2026-10-26): **(a)** — detach both children. Applied: `LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG` and `LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X` now have `parentId=null` and carry `discovered-from:LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ` in their descriptions (their own `intake_complete` stage and their dep edge T8→U2 are preserved). Source: producer reply to the intake question comment.
- Q2 (code name — resolved): AC2's example `local_admission_refused` vs the shipped `local_admission_reject` (`EXHAUSTION_CODE_LOCAL_ADMISSION`, `provider.py:5518`, already used end-to-end by LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL and asserted in `test_admission_reserve.py:461`). data.description:
# Local-only admission refusal is invisible in proxy logs and logs a false fallback line

## Headline

A `local-only` admission refusal returns the 429 to the client but leaves **no countable trace** in `proxy.log`, and the `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line is logged *before* the local-only branch returns, so the log claims routing that never happened.

## Problem statement

When the local admission guard refuses a request pinned to `X-Local-Preference: local-only`, the proxy returns the retryable 429 without ever logging the refusal itself. The only traces are the guard's own `local_admission_guard decision=reject …` line (indistinguishable from a `prefer-local` refusal that *did* fall through and succeed remotely) and a false `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line that states the opposite of what happened. Operators cannot count or alert on this failure class, and log-based diagnosis of these 429s mis-attributes them to chain exhaustion.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / triage agent** — must be able to attribute a client-visible 429 to "local-only admission refused" from `proxy.log` alone.
- **Monitoring analyst** — consumes log tokens for alerting/trending (`proxy-usage-analysis`, runbooks); needs a stable, countable token for this failure class.
- **`proxy-log-debug` skill / runbook readers** — grep stable log tokens documented in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

User stories:

- As a triage agent diagnosing a `429 "All providers exhausted"`-style client error, I want to grep one token and see every local-only refusal with its reason and budget evidence, so I can tell "local refused the request by design" from "the chain really ran out".
- As an operator, I want the log to never claim "routing to next provider" for a request that was refused, so fallback accounting is truthful.

## Observed behaviour (verified 2026-10-27 against `dev` HEAD)

Diagnosing session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` (429 "All providers exhausted") required grepping `proxy.log` for chain-exhaustion events that never existed: the refusal leaves no refusal line at all, while a *false* fallback line is emitted for it.

```
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=true  session=herdr-1792897705-…
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard_direct_fallback provider=local-qwen3 … → routing to next provider
              ← nothing was routed: the local-only branch returns the 429
```

Verified current code (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`):

- `provider.py:11014–11024` logs `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback provider=… model=… session=… reason=… free_slot=true → routing to next provider` **before** the `_preference == _PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` branch at `provider.py:11026`, which for local-only returns the 429 (`:11032`, `_build_exhausted_response`). The log states the opposite of what happened for the local-only case.
- Three return sites hand a local-only refusal to the client today:
  - contention-queue path: `provider.py:10426` → `_build_local_only_refusal_response` (429);
  - direct guard path: `provider.py:11032` → `_build_exhausted_response` (429);
  - lease path: `provider.py:11422` → `_build_local_only_refusal_response` (429).
- None of the three sites logs the refusal itself; the only common token is the guard's `local_admission_guard decision=reject …` line (`prefill_eta.py:1296`), shared with `prefer-local` refusals that fall through and succeed remotely.
- No `local_only_refusal` token exists anywhere in `proxy/`; `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the guard decision line and `X-Local-Route: refused` header but no greppable refusal token.
- Existing tests assert the misleading line *is present* (prefer-local path only, `test_local_admission_guard.py:692–697`); there are **no** tests referencing `refused_local_only` or any local-only refusal log line.

Note: the original description's line numbers (direct `:10432`/`:10450`, contention `:10785`) are stale — the code moved; the behaviour they describe is unchanged and still present.

## Goal

Every local-only admission refusal is attributable from the proxy log alone, and no log line claims routing that did not happen.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line is emitted only on an actual fall-through to the next provider. For a local-only refusal it is either not emitted or clearly qualified — never with "→ routing to next provider" wording.
2. Each local-only refusal emits exactly one INFO line with stable `key=value` fields, e.g.
   `local_only_refusal session=… provider=… reason=… new_tokens=… budget_tokens=… eta_prefill_seconds=… budget_seconds=… priority=… route=refused`,
   on **every** refusal path (contention-queue `provider.py:10426`, direct guard `provider.py:11032`, lease `provider.py:11422`). All fields must come from the admission decision actually used at that site (fields are already carried on the decision object logged at `prefill_eta.py:1296`). The existing guard `local_admission_guard decision=…` line remains unchanged (shared with `prefer-local`), so refusals are counted by `local_only_refusal`, not by `decision=reject`.
3. The refusal is countable from the log by a single stable token — `local_only_refusal` — and `proxy/docs/routing.md` (Observability section) documents the token so runbooks and the `proxy-log-debug` skill can grep it.
4. Tests:
   - a test asserting the `local_only_refusal` log line is emitted for a local-only refusal on each path (contention-queue, direct guard, lease);
   - a test asserting the misleading "→ routing to next provider" line is **not** emitted for a refused local-only request on the direct path;
   - a test asserting a `prefer-local` fall-through still emits the existing `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line (regression guard for `test_local_admission_guard.py:692`).
5. Verification note: the 2026-10-25 11:57:09 case (guard rejection of `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152`) is reproducible in a test, and the resulting log output is shown in the work item.

## Constraints

- No change to the 429 response contract (body/headers) — response-text consistency is the sibling item **LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ**, pending there.
- No change to `prefer-local` fall-through behaviour.
- No change to the guard's own `local_admission_guard decision=…` line (stable tokens at `prefill_eta.py:1296`).
- Logging must never break routing: refusals log from inside the already-returned branch (best-effort, in the pattern of `_note_local_fallback_reason`).

## Assumptions (documented)

- "Exactly one INFO line" (AC2) means exactly one `local_only_refusal` line per refused request; the guard's `decision=reject` line and any `Fallback triggered` lines for genuine fall-throughs are unchanged and not counted as refusal lines.
- Quality of the line is what matters for counting: the token must be greppable and stable; field names mirror the guard decision's existing keys (`new_tokens`, `budget_tokens`, `eta_prefill_seconds`, `budget_seconds`, `projected_wait_seconds` where available).
- Updating the `proxy-log-debug` skill (`.pi/skills/…`) is out of scope (repo-boundary rule); documenting the token in `proxy/docs/routing.md` satisfies AC3 and the skill can be updated as a follow-up work item.

## Risks

- **Merge/behavioural overlap with sibling `LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ`** — both touch the direct-guard return block (`provider.py:11026–11032`). Sequence the two items (or implement together) to avoid conflicting edits; this item only moves/quotes the log line, it does not change the response. If `LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ` lands first and switches the direct path to `_build_local_only_refusal_response`, AC2's site list still holds (the log line goes at the same branch).
- **Scope creep risk** — logging-related opportunities (e.g. request-header logging for `X-Local-Preference`, `proxy-log-debug` skill update) are recorded below as related work/out of scope, not added to this item.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the three refusal return sites (`:10426`, `:11032`, `:11422`) and the misleading log (`:11014–11024`); add the `local_only_refusal` INFO line just inside each local-only refusal branch, and move/qualify the fallback log.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — Observability section (`~:1051`) documents the decision line; add the `local_only_refusal` token.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — extend for direct-path refusal and prefer-local regression (`:692–697`); add direct-path non-emission test.
- `proxy/tests/…` — coverage for contention-queue and lease refusal paths (existing local-only tests are absent; the cq/lease harnesses already used by `test_hard_routing_cap.py`/`test_prefill_eta.py` can be reused).

## Related work

- `LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ` (in progress, same session) — local-only refusal must not report "All providers exhausted" (response body/headers contract; complementary, same 2026-10-25 case).
- `LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG` (open) — local-only intent is only enforced at the admission guard; skip paths silently fall through to remote (enforcement, not logging).
- `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (completed) — introduced X-Local-Preference/X-Local-Route, the local-only refusal response and `_build_local_only_refusal_response`.
- `LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ`, `LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7`, `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` (completed) — prefill-ETA admission guard, cold-prefill budget enforcement, occupancy-aware deadline admission: the guard whose reject line is the only current trace.
- `LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM` (completed) — AC7 eviction event truthfulness (same observability theme: logged values must reflect the admission decision).
- `LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO` (completed) — overnight remote-chain exhaustion diagnostics (the failure class this refusal is currently mis-attributed to).
- Duplicate check performed (2026-10-27): no overlapping completed item found — no item covers local-only refusal logging.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- No interactive interview round was needed: the seed context (2026-10-25 diagnosis summary plus acceptance criteria) sufficed to draft the brief. Two assumptions were documented above instead of asked (see "Assumptions (documented)") — both are conservative readings of the existing AC text. If the producer prefers a different reading (e.g. the guard's own `decision=reject` line should also be suppressed for local-only refusals, or the token should count per-path occurrences), amend AC2 before planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)
- **LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ** – Local-only admission refusal must not report 'All providers exhausted' (in-progress)
- **LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG** – local-only intent is only enforced at the admission guard — skip paths silently fall through to remote (open)

### Repository file matches (trimmed)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the refusal sites and the misleading fallback line (full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ.md`; two `ds4/gguf-tools/…rendered_prompts*.txt` matches were corpus noise and are omitted here).

data.description:
## Problem

The local-only refusal **does** advertise a retry timer today, but it is untruthful for the reason that actually fires.

`_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`provider.py:5521`) and `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`provider.py:6310`) both compute:

```python
retry_after = suggested_retry_after_seconds(eta_prefill_seconds, budget_seconds, maximum=...)
# prefill_eta.py:1204
delay = int(math.ceil(max(0.0, eta - budget)))      # "how much LONGER than your budget"
return max(1, min(int(maximum or 1), delay))         # floor of 1 second
```

For the 2026-10-25 incident (`reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`, `eta_prefill_s=0.0`, `budget_s=60.0`, `new_tokens=31246`, `budget_tokens=25000`) that yields **`Retry-After: 1`** and `"retry_after": 1` in the body. That is wrong twice over:

1. Waiting cannot help: the prompt is permanently over the flat `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` cap. A 1-second hint invites exactly the retry storm that was observed — the client backed off 7 times (up to 2 m 8 s) and then reported the 429 as non-retryable.
2. The hint has no absolute time and no reason-specific meaning: for `eta_exceeds_budget` it describes "how much longer than *your* wait budget the prefill would take", not when local capacity becomes available, and it is capped without any `X-Local-Admission-*` token evidence the client can act on.

A retry time does exist for the *other* availability causes, but on a different code path: `_compute_retry_after()` (`provider.py:4242`) derives an honest value from real cooldowns, `available_times` edges and usage-limit resets. A local-only client whose local entry is skipped for a non-admission reason (cooldown, `context_too_large`, contention-queue expiry) therefore gets a *different* timer semantics from the refusal path — and, worse, in the cooldown case the request is currently allowed to fall through to a remote provider, silently breaking the local-only contract (`local-only` is enforced only at the admission decision: `provider.py:6753`, `:11027`).

## Goal

A local-only request that cannot be served locally answers with a retry hint that is truthful for its reason: a real wait time where waiting helps, an explicit "not time-retryable, compact instead" where it cannot help, and an absolute timestamp a scheduler can use.

## Users

- **local-only clients** (herdr worker sessions pinned with `X-Local-Preference: local-only`) that currently retry "1 second" seven times before giving up.
  - As a local-only client, I want a refusal to tell me *whether* waiting helps and *when* to retry, so I never hammer the proxy pointlessly or misreported a recoverable 429 as terminal.
- **Schedulers / dispatch layers** acting on `Retry-After`.
  - As a blocker, I want `retry_at` (absolute RFC 3339 UTC) so I need not trust my own clock.
- **Proxy operators** triaging `proxy.log` refusal bursts.
  - As an operator, I want the token-headers on every refusal so a client that compacts can be told exactly how far over budget it was.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded` (uncached tokens over the flat cap) is reported as **not time-retryable**: no `Retry-After` header, `"retry_after": null`, `"retryable": false`, `"new_tokens"`/`"budget_tokens"` in the body, and the `suggested_action` names compaction as the remedy.
2. Occupancy/ETA refusals (`eta_exceeds_budget`, `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`) return `Retry-After` = `ceil(projected_wait_seconds - budget_seconds)` (min 1 s, capped by `server.max_retry_after_seconds`), and the body carries both `retry_after` (seconds) and `retry_at` (RFC 3339 UTC) so clients need not trust their own clock.
3. When the local entry is unavailable for a non-admission reason (cooldown, lease held, `context_too_large`, contention-queue expiry), the retry hint is derived from the real expiry (`_compute_retry_after` / cooldown remaining / lease remaining), not from the ETA formula.
4. `X-Local-Admission-New-Tokens` and `X-Local-Admission-Budget-Tokens` are emitted on both refusal paths so a client can decide to compact rather than retry.
5. `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the per-reason retry contract (when to wait, when to compact, when to allow remote), including `retry_at` and the 429/`X-Local-Route: refused` shape.
6. Tests: table-driven unit coverage per reason asserting status, `retry_after`/`retry_at`/header presence-or-absence, and the token headers; a regression test that the 2026-10-25 `prefill_budget_exceeded` case emits **no** `Retry-After`; a test that a cooldown-driven refusal advertises the cooldown remainder.
7. Verification note: reproduce the 11:57:09 UTC refusal in a test and show the returned headers/body in the work item.

## Constraints

- `suggested_retry_after_seconds()` (`prefill_eta.py:1204`) is the shared estimator used by both builders today; the fix must move both refusal paths onto reason-aware timing (AC2/AC3) without changing `_compute_retry_after()`'s existing callers (chain-hold / exhaustion paths keep using it as-is).
- `server.max_retry_after_seconds` (`_max_retry_after_seconds()`, `provider.py:4403`) remains the ceiling for any advertised duration.
- The body additions (`retry_at`, `retryable`, token counts) are **additive**: old clients that only read `retry_after`/`error`/`code` must not break; exhaustion-code contract (LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G) stays untouched.
- `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded` must carry the token evidence the guard actually used (`new_tokens=31246` vs `budget_tokens=25000` in the incident) — thread it from the admission decision, do not recompute.

## Existing state

- Both refusal builders (`provider.py:5521`, `:6310`) call `suggested_retry_after_seconds()` (ETA-minus-budget, floor 1 s); `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded` currently gets `Retry-After: 1`.
- `retry_at`/`retryable`/token headers do not exist on either path; `X-Local-Admission-*` headers today are `Eta`/`Budget` only (`provider.py:5550`, `:6344`).
- Honest timers exist only on the non-refusal exhaust path via `_compute_retry_after()` (`provider.py:4242`) and cooldown/lease expiry data; the refusal paths never consult them.

## Desired change

- Refactor both refusal builders around a single reason→timing decision: `prefill_budget_exceeded` → no `Retry-After` + `retryable:false` + compaction guidance; ETA/occupancy reasons → `ceil(wait-budget)` + `retry_at`; non-admission skips → real expiry (cooldown/lease/`_compute_retry_after`).
- Thread `new_tokens`/`budget_tokens` from `_local_admission_decision` into the refusal builders and emit them as `X-Local-Admission-New-Tokens` / `X-Local-Admission-Budget-Tokens` (and body fields).
- Add the verification test reproducing 11:57:09 UTC (`new_tokens=31246`, `budget_tokens=25000`) and assert no `Retry-After`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`:5521`), `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`:6310`), `_max_retry_after_seconds()` (`:4403`), `_compute_retry_after()` (`:4242`), enforcement points (`:6753`, `:11027`), `_note_local_fallback_reason()` (`:6286`), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (`:6387`).
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `suggested_retry_after_seconds()` (`:1204`) — the estimator to be made reason-aware (or bypassed per reason).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — the `new_tokens`/`budget_tokens` evidence source on the admission decision (cold-prefill budget, LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — table-driven reason tests + the 2026-10-25 regression.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — per-reason retry contract documentation (AC5).

## Related work

- LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ (parent) — same-shape refusal contract; this item refines the *timing* semantics inside that shape.
- LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG — local-only enforcement on all skip paths (blocking this item's AC3/when-to-wait data: a cooldown skip must refuse rather than fall through); this item depends on it.
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 — cold-prefill budget implementation (the `budget_tokens` source).
- LP-0MV0MM5R60025XZE — retry-timer cap at 60 min (completed) — the historical `maximum` precedent.
- LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G — stable exhaustion codes (completed) — kept byte-compatible per Constraints.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the parent (LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ) and sibling (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG) land first or concurrently; the single refusal-shape builder from the parent is the natural home for the reason-aware timing.
- Risk: emitting no `Retry-After` for `prefill_budget_exceeded` changes client behaviour (they may retry immediately on absence). Mitigation: `retryable:false` + explicit compaction in `suggested_action`; document in routing.md.
- Risk: `retry_at` computed from ETA vs real capacity can still be optimistic. Mitigation: cap by `max_retry_after_seconds`, and for non-admission skips prefer the real expiry.
- Scope-creep guard: changing the *numeric value* of `Retry-After` for exhaustion paths (as opposed to the refusal paths) is out of scope — only refusal-path timing changes here.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: For `prefill_budget_exceeded`, should the response omit `Retry-After` entirely or set it to a long fixed value? — Answer: infer **omit entirely** with `retryable:false` (AC1), since any timer misleads the client; recorded as authored intent, no interactive answer received.
- Q: Should `retry_at` be added to the exhaustion responses too (not just refusals)? — Answer: **no** — scope is the local-only refusal paths (AC2); exhaustion responses keep their existing contract (LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G) untouched.

## Provenance

discovered-from:LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ — discovered while triaging LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ (Local-only admission refusal must not report 'All providers exhausted').
Tracked as a separate item by producer decision 2026-10-26 (the defects are distinct: this item's scope is not part of that bug's acceptance criteria).



## Plan

**Parent:** LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X — Local-only refusal: truthful, reason-specific retry time
**Planned:** 2026-10-27 | **Effort:** Small | **Risk:** Medium | **Approval gate:** not required (not XL+High)
**AC coverage:** 7/7 parent ACs mapped to children (tree-coverage review: 100%, `proceed`)

### Per-reason retry contract (target behaviour)

| Reason | `Retry-After` | `retryable` | `retry_at` | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prefill_budget_exceeded` | **absent** | `false` | absent | compact the prompt |
| `eta_exceeds_budget`, `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget` | `ceil(wait - budget)`, min 1 s, capped | `true` | RFC 3339 UTC | wait (`Retry-After`) |
| cooldown / lease-held / contention-queue expiry (non-admission skip) | real expiry remainder | `true` | RFC 3339 UTC | wait |
| `context_too_large` | **absent** | `false` | absent | compact the prompt |

Every refusal also carries `X-Local-Admission-New-Tokens` / `X-Local-Admission-Budget-Tokens`
(and body equivalents) plus `X-Local-Route: refused`.

### Child work items (test-first order)

| # | ID | Title | Type | Pri | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LP-0MVQ239VQ001RXZ0 | Test: AC1 regression — `prefill_budget_exceeded` emits no `Retry-After` | task | high | AC1, AC7 | — |
| 2 | LP-0MVQ23A6S007DVDM | Test: AC2 — ETA/occupancy refusals return `Retry-After` + `retry_at` | task | high | AC2, AC4 | — |
| 3 | LP-0MVQ23AGI006JNH4 | Test: AC6 — table-driven unit tests per reason + cooldown refusal test | task | high | AC6 | — |
| 4 | LP-0MVQ23API001UOET | Refactor: reason-aware timing decision for refusal paths | task | high | AC1, AC2 | 1, 2, 3 |
| 5 | LP-0MVQ23AYQ000CGTW | Refactor: thread token evidence into refusal builders | task | medium | AC4 | 3 |
| 6 | LP-0MVQ23B80009OZ9V | Refactor: non-admission skip retry timing (**BLOCKED**) | task | medium | AC3 | 3, LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG |
| 7 | LP-0MVQ23BH7006HLKB | Documentation: per-reason retry contract in `routing.md` | task | medium | AC5 | 4, 5 |

### Phases (vertical slices)

- **Phase 1 — red tests:** children 1–3. Each writes failing tests through the
  full path (request → routing → 429 shape → headers/body). Deliverable: failing
  suite that pins the new contract.
- **Phase 2 — core timing:** child 4 (single reason→timing helper used by **both**
  refusal builders) + child 5 (token evidence threading). Deliverable: AC1/AC2/AC4
  green; `prefill_budget_exceeded` emits no `Retry-After`.
- **Phase 3 — non-admission skips:** child 6, unblocked only when
  LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG lands (cooldown skips must refuse rather than fall through;
  today they silently go remote). Deliverable: AC3 green.
- **Phase 4 — contract docs:** child 7. Deliverable: AC5 documented.
  Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update it with any
  learned detail (e.g. exact `attempt` dict keys) before implementing.

### Reuse (no new machinery)

- `_compute_retry_after()` (`provider.py:4261`) is reused as-is for
  cooldown/`available_times`/`_usage_reset_at` expiry; existing callers untouched.
- `_max_retry_after_seconds()` (`provider.py:~4403`) stays the ceiling.
- `attempt["retry_after_s"]` already overrides the ETA formula in
  `_build_local_only_refusal_response` — the non-admission path can thread the
  real expiry through it rather than adding a second branch.
- `attempt["projected_wait_seconds"]` is already populated for the ETA reasons.
- `secrets.X-Local-Route` stamping already exists (`_stamp_local_route_headers`).

### Risks carried into implementation

- No `Retry-After` on `prefill_budget_exceeded` may cause immediate client retries:

- `retry_at` from ETA can be optimistic: capped by `max_retry_after_seconds`; real

data.description:
## Problem

`X-Local-Preference: local-only` is enforced in **exactly two** places — the admission decisions at `provider.py:6753` (contention-queue path, `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`) and `provider.py:11027` (direct/lease path, inside `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`). Every other reason the local entry is dropped from the chain simply `continue`s to the next provider, so a client that pinned its work to the local GPU can be served by a paid remote provider **without any signal** to the client or the log.

`_request_local_preference()` call sites (`grep` over `proxy/proxy/provider.py`):

```
6305 def _request_local_preference(...)
6753   ← enforced (queue admission, _maybe_queue_for_local_slot)
9517   ← log only (priority_routing, _proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle)
11027  ← enforced (direct admission, _proxy_with_fallback_cycle)
```

Skip paths that ignore it (all end in `continue` → next provider):

| Path | Log line | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Local entry in cooldown | `Skipping provider=local-qwen3: local-qwen3 in cooldown (675s remaining)` | `provider.py:7160` |
| Router skip (context too large, resident prefix insufficient, prefill thrash cooldown, economic/idle bypass) | `routing_skip_local … reason=… → skipping local, routing to next remote provider` | `provider.py:10739`, `:10271` |
| Contention-queue caps exceeded / queue expiry | `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue … queued_duration=…` | `provider.py:10355`, `:11358` |
| Prefill gate / lease denied (actions other than `refused_local_only`) | `local_dispatch_denied …`, `prefill_gate_wait_ms=…` | lease/gate branches |
| Local entry context cap (`max_context_tokens`) / quota hard stop | `routing_skip_provider_context …`, `Skipping provider=…: <quota stop reason>` | `provider.py:3325`, `:7160` |

Note the asymmetry: the opposite intent (`remote-ok`) *is* enforced structurally — `apply_local_preference()` strips local entries from the chain (`proxy/proxy/priority.py:410`) — so only `local-only` can leak.

## Evidence (2026-10-25)

Session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` sent `X-Local-Preference: local-only` (confirmed on its 11:46–11:57 requests) and was nonetheless served by **OpenCode Go** at 11:32:47, 11:33:35 and 11:34:48 while its local route was contended/skipped (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`, `routing_resident_prefix … decision=resident_prefix_insufficient`). It is not possible to prove the header was on those three requests because request headers are never logged, and `priority_routing … preference=` carries no session id — hence AC5 below.

## Goal

A `local-only` request either completes locally or receives the local-only refusal — it is never silently served by a remote provider, and any deviation is attributable from the log.

## Users

- **herdr worker sessions** that pin `X-Local-Preference: local-only` to keep paid-remote costs at zero (e.g. the 2026-10-25 session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152`). With this defect, they are billed for remote serve without consent.
  - As a local-only client, I want every local-skip reason to end in the refusal (`429` + `X-Local-Route: refused`), so the proxy never silently spends my remote budget.
- **Proxy operators** reading `proxy.log`.
  - As an operator, I want each skip/fallback decision to log the parsed preference, so a local-only violation is attributable to a session without header-correlation heuristics.

## Acceptance criteria

1. With `X-Local-Preference: local-only`, **no** remote provider is dispatched for any skip reason: cooldown, router skip (`context_too_large`, `resident_prefix_insufficient`, `prefill_thrash_cooldown`, economic/idle bypass), contention-queue cap/expiry, prefill-gate or lease denial, entry context cap, quota hard stop.
2. Each of those outcomes returns the local-only refusal response (429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <skip reason>`) rather than falling through; the reason the local route was unavailable is carried in the body/headers.
3. `prefer-local` (default) behaviour is unchanged for every one of those paths — it still falls through to the next provider exactly as today.
4. Every skip/fallback line that decides "not local" logs the parsed preference (`preference=local-only|prefer-local|remote-ok`) so an intent violation is visible in `proxy.log`; `priority_routing` keeps its existing fields (additive change only).
5. Attribution is possible: the `priority_routing …` line (or its successor) carries the session id / request id, so a preference can be tied to a specific request without correlation heuristics.
6. Tests: one test per skip reason asserting local-only ⇒ refusal and prefer-local ⇒ remote dispatch (table-driven); a regression test asserting `remote-ok` still strips local; a test asserting the preference appears on the skip/fallback log line.
7. `proxy/docs/routing.md` states that `local-only` is enforced on every exit from the local route, not only at the admission guard.

## Constraints

- `prefer-local` (the default for every client that does not send the header) must remain byte-compatible with today's fall-through behaviour on all paths.
- The refusal response shape must match the sibling item LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ (same 429 / `X-Local-Route: refused` / headers / body contract) so clients discriminate on one stable shape; see that item's `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`provider.py:6310`).
- No new config knobs required unless a skip reason genuinely cannot wait: prefer-local-only refusals to carry the existing refusal headers.
- `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` must carry a stable per-reason token (matching log `reason=` values) so clients can classify without parsing prose.

## Existing state

- `local-only` enforced only at the two admission decisions (`provider.py:6753`, `:11027`); every other skip `continue`s to remote.
- `remote-ok` enforced structurally by `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:410`); chain-emptied case falls through to the exhaustion path unchanged.
- Refusal builders already exist and are tested: `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`provider.py:6310`) on the contention-queue paths; the direct-lease path currently funnels through `_build_exhausted_response()` → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` (see LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ — the two paths disagree on `error` text).

## Desired change

- Introduce a single local-only refusal choke point (or reuse `_build_local_only_refusal_response`) so every `continue` that would otherwise leave the local route short-circuits to the refusal when `_request_local_preference(request) == "local-only"`.
- Log `preference=<parsed>` on each skip/fallback line (additive to existing fields) and thread the session/request id into `priority_routing`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_request_local_preference()` (`:6305`), enforcement points (`:6753`, `:11027`), skip paths (`:7160`, `:10271`, `:10355`, `:10739`, `:11358`), refusal builders (`:6310`, `:5521`), `_note_local_fallback_reason()` (`:6286`), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (`:6387`).
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `apply_local_preference()` (`:410`), `local_preference_for_request()` (`:398`) — structural `remote-ok` filter, the model for making `local-only` structural too.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `parse_preference()` (`:415`), the canonical header parser (`local-only`/`prefer-local`/`remote-ok`, unknown → `prefer-local`).
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — existing refusal-path tests; table-driven per-skip-reason tests are added here.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `X-Local-Preference` semantics (`:1158`), `X-Local-Route` values (`:1173`); AC7 doc update lands here.

## Related work

- LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ (parent) — same-shape refusal contract; this item extends enforcement from the two guard sites to every skip path.
- LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL — introduced `X-Local-Preference` + AC4 refusal mechanics (completed).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (completed).
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 — cold-prefill budget enforcement (completed).
- LP-0MVI63OM1009K51W — lease-owner retention grace (blocked).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the two refusal paths converge on the LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ shape *before* or *with* this item; if that parent lands first, this item reuses its builder.
- Risk: turning every skip into a refusal changes latency/UX for legitimate local-only requests (they will now 429 instead of silently completing remotely). Mitigation: `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` + docs so clients can decide to compact/allow remote; the refusal is the honest outcome the client opted into.
- Risk: log-grep tooling depends on existing `priority_routing` fields; mitigation: additive changes only, keep field names stable.
- Scope-creep guard: queueing/leasing redesign, per-skip cancellation of in-flight remote dispatch, and billing-affinity changes are out of scope — record as new items if they surface.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should every skip reason (including hard config caps like `max_context_tokens`) refuse, or only transient capacity reasons? — Answer: infer **all skip reasons** from AC1's explicit enumeration (cooldown, router skip, contention cap/expiry, prefill-gate/lease denial, context cap, quota hard stop); a client that pinned local-only expects no remote dispatch for any reason. Recorded as authored intent; no interactive answer received.
- Q: Does the direct-lease path need a separate refusal builder, or reuse the queue path's `_build_local_only_refusal_response`? — Answer: reuse a single builder for one stable shape (aligned with LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ AC1). Implementation detail; no interactive answer received.

## Provenance

discovered-from:LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ — discovered while triaging LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ (Local-only admission refusal must not report 'All providers exhausted').
Tracked as a separate item by producer decision 2026-10-26 (the defects are distinct: this item's scope is not part of that bug's acceptance criteria).
